Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the group business continuity plan set required by ICP 8 Standard 8.3; escalates any critical function without an achievable recovery time objective to the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - ICP 8 (Risk Management and Internal Controls) Standard 8.3 and ICP 16 (ERM for Solvency Purposes) Standards 16.1 and 16.14 re-read in the consolidated ICP text on iaisweb.org at review start, then traced to the binding local transpositions (PRA SS1/21 operational resilience, EU DORA Articles 11-12, BMA Operational Cyber Risk Management Code) because ICPs bind supervisors, not the insurer directly

In-scope processes.value: The policyholder-facing critical functions named in the business impact analysis: claims notification and claim payment, policy administration and premium collection, annuity and death-benefit disbursement, actuarial valuation close, treasury settlement and reinsurance recovery - each carrying its own RTO/RPO

In-scope systems.value: Business Continuity module holding the BIA register, plan library, RTO/RPO register and plan-owner attestations; approved plan PDFs published to the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Group Business Continuity Policy plus one Business Continuity Plan per critical function and one IT Disaster Recovery Plan per supporting platform, each carrying BIA outputs, RTO/RPO, invocation criteria, recovery team roster, dependency map and manual workaround

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved annually by the Board Risk Committee on the Chief Risk Officer's recommendation; out-of-cycle re-approval whenever a critical function's RTO changes or a new critical function goes live

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual plan review closed before the Board Risk Committee Q4 papers deadline; BIA refresh within 30 days of a new critical function going live; plan update within 30 days of any material change to a supporting application or outsourced provider

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow tasks fire to each plan owner at T-90, T-45 and T-15 days against the Board Risk Committee papers deadline, with automatic escalation to the Operational Resilience Lead at T-15

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved plan versions, BIA worksheets, dependency maps, plan-owner attestations and Board Risk Committee minutes retained 7 years from the date the plan version is superseded

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A critical function with no approved plan, a plan older than 12 months, or an RTO with no evidenced recovery capability is raised as a resilience issue with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs off closure of every out-of-tolerance critical function and every plan that missed its annual review date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every critical business service on the BIA register at the review date, its supporting applications from the CMDB, and every plan version issued during the year

Three or more failing critical functions escalates to the Board Risk Committee as a control weakness.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous maintenance on an annual review cycle, so the test runs annually ahead of Board approval, plus a half-year interim check limited to functions whose applications, providers or RTOs changed since the last review

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the business continuity and IT operations functions and must not own or have authored any sampled plan

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual BCP adequacy workpaper (BIA extract, plan sample, RTO substantiation, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository and indexed by critical function name

Regulator-ready documentation.value: ICP 8.3 self-assessment pack - BIA register, plan inventory with approval dates, dependency and third-party map, latest recovery test results - assembled for a group-wide supervisor college or IMF FSAP request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager coordinates the group-wide supervisor's request and the supervisory college pack; the Chief Risk Officer clears any statement about recovery capability or RTO achievement before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Refresh the business impact analysis for every critical function
actions: In the GRC platform open Business Continuity, Business Impact Analysis and filter Status = 'Due for review' by review-cycle year.

For each critical function interview the process owner (Claims Director / Manager for claim payment, Policy Admin Ops Lead for policy servicing, Treasury Manager for settlement) and record peak daily volumes, peak day of the month and the maximum tolerable period of disruption.
Quantify the policyholder harm per outage duration band (4h / 24h / 72h / 1 week): unpaid claims count and value, missed annuity payment runs, lapsed policies from unprocessed premium.
Enter the harm figures in the BIA record and attach the process owner's email confirmation as the source.
Close out functions the business no longer performs by marking the BIA record Retired with a reason, so the register does not carry ghost functions.
checklist.done: every critical function has a BIA record dated in the current cycle with quantified harm by outage band and a named process owner.

checklist.step: Set recovery time and recovery point objectives and the impact tolerance per function
actions: Convert each BIA maximum tolerable period of disruption into an RTO (hours to restore the service) and an RPO (maximum acceptable data loss in hours) on the RTO/RPO register.
Set the impact tolerance as a plain sentence naming the outer limit - for example 'claim payments resume within 24 hours and no payment instruction issued in the prior 4 hours is lost'.
Take the Chief Financial Officer's confirmation that the liquidity buffer supports benefit payments through the tolerance window, and file the reply.
Where the RTO the business wants is shorter than what IT Operations can evidence, record the gap on the register rather than writing the aspiration into the plan.
Hand the agreed RTO/RPO table to the Disaster Recovery Manager as the design constraint for the DR plans.
checklist.done: each critical function carries an agreed RTO, RPO and one-sentence impact tolerance, with any capability gap recorded rather than hidden.

checklist.step: Map each critical function to its supporting applications, infrastructure and data
actions: In the CMDB open the business service record for the function and list every downstream configuration item: application, database, integration, hosting region and network path.
Cross-check the list against the actual production call graph with the Site Reliability Engineer so shadow dependencies (batch jobs, file drops, reporting extracts) are captured.
Record for each application its recovery tier, hosting model (on-premise, private cloud, SaaS) and the data classification of what it holds.
Flag any single points of failure - one region, one payment file transfer, one authentication provider - on the dependency map.
Attach the dependency map to the function's BIA record in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: each critical function has a current dependency map naming every supporting application, its recovery tier and its single points of failure.

checklist.step: Pull the third-party and intragroup dependencies into the plan
actions: Extract from the contract repository every provider supporting an in-scope critical function: TPA claims handlers, print/mail vendors, payment processors, cloud hosting, actuarial software hosting and intragroup shared services.
Read each contract's service levels, exit and step-in clauses and business continuity obligations, and record the contractual recovery commitment against the function's RTO.
Request each provider's most recent BCP summary and DR test attestation from the Vendor Manager and file it with the contract record.
Where a provider commitment is weaker than the internal RTO, record it as a resilience issue and name the substitutability option (alternate provider, in-house workaround, deferred processing).
Feed the confirmed provider list back to the register maintained under REG-013-C51 so the two records cannot diverge.
checklist.done: every critical function names its providers, their contractual recovery commitments and a substitutability option for those that fall short of the RTO.

checklist.step: Write or refresh the business continuity plan for each critical function
actions: Open the plan template in the document management repository and populate: scope, RTO/RPO, impact tolerance, invocation criteria, recovery team with named primaries and alternates, and the hour-by-hour recovery sequence for the first 24 hours.
Write the manual workaround explicitly - which forms, which spreadsheets, which approval limits apply when the primary system is unavailable, and who signs.
Name the relocation or remote-working arrangement for the recovery team and the minimum headcount required to run the workaround.
Insert the dependency map and the provider list produced in the earlier steps as appendices rather than re-typing them.
Version the document as <function>-BCP-v<n>-<yyyy-mm-dd> and set the owner and next review date in the document properties.
checklist.done: each critical function has a versioned plan carrying invocation criteria, a named recovery team, a 24-hour recovery sequence and a written manual workaround.

checklist.step: Write the IT disaster recovery plan behind each recovery tier
actions: For each tier-1 application on the dependency map, document the recovery architecture: standby region, replication method, replication lag, failover trigger and the runbook reference.
Record the technical RPO the replication actually delivers (measured lag, not the design target) and compare it to the business RPO from the register.

Write the failover and failback runbook steps with the exact console paths - for example the cloud console region failover screen, the database promote command and the DNS or load-balancer cutover record to change.
Name the restore-from-backup path for data corruption scenarios, including the backup retention depth and the last successful restore date.
Link the DR plan to the business continuity plan of every function that depends on the application.
checklist.done: each tier-1 application has a DR plan with a measured RPO, a failover runbook and a linked restore-from-backup path.

checklist.step: Fix the invocation criteria, escalation ladder and crisis-management call tree
actions: Write the objective triggers that invoke the plan - for example claim payment file not issued for 4 hours, policy administration unavailable for 2 hours in a business day, or confirmed data loss in a tier-1 system.
Name who can invoke at each level (duty manager, Operational Risk Manager, Chief Operating Officer) and what authority invocation confers over spend and staffing.
Build the crisis management team call tree with primary and alternate contacts, out-of-hours numbers and a non-corporate communication channel that survives loss of the corporate network.
Set the standing cadence for crisis calls once invoked (every 2 hours for the first 12 hours, then 4-hourly) and name the scribe who keeps the decision log.
Circulate the call tree to the Incident Response Lead so security incidents and operational disruptions escalate onto the same bridge.
checklist.done: objective invocation triggers, named invocation authorities and a tested out-of-band call tree are recorded in every plan.

checklist.step: Prove the claims and benefit payment workaround will actually pay policyholders
actions: With Treasury, document the degraded payment path: manual payment instruction template, dual-authorisation limits, the bank channel used when the claims platform cannot generate the payment file, and the daily value cap.
Record how claim decisions are captured offline (numbered manual claim register) and how they are replayed into the claims platform once service returns, including the duplicate-payment check.
Agree with the Chief Claims Officer the hardship criteria for prioritising payments during a disruption - death claims and annuity income before routine servicing.
Rehearse the manual instruction with the Treasury Manager on a single non-production payment and file the confirmation.
Attach the workaround pack to the claims BCP as the appendix the recovery team actually opens.
checklist.done: the degraded claim-payment path is documented, authority limits are agreed and a rehearsed manual instruction is on file.

checklist.step: Write the policyholder, distributor and regulator communication plan for a disruption
actions: Draft holding statements for the contact centre, the customer self-service portal banner and the broker portal, one per scenario band (system unavailable, data incident, site loss).
Agree with the Contact Center Ops Manager the overflow arrangements and the script for telling policyholders when a claim or payment will be handled.
Name the notification obligations to supervisors and the person who owns them, cross-referencing the incident reporting procedure under REG-013-C52.
Get the General Counsel to pre-clear each holding statement so nothing needs legal drafting during the first hour of an event.
File the approved statements in the plan appendix with a last-cleared date.
checklist.done: pre-cleared holding statements exist for each scenario band with named channel owners and a supervisor notification owner.

checklist.step: Reconcile the plans to the ERM framework and the ORSA operational risk view
actions: Compare the operational risk scenarios used in the ORSA (site loss, cyber outage, key provider failure) with the scenarios the plans actually cover and list any scenario with no plan behind it.
Confirm the residual operational risk rating in the risk register reflects the recovery capability evidenced, not the aspirational RTO.
Feed the resilience issues log into the ORSA operational risk section so the capital and management-action narrative matches the plan reality.
Record the reconciliation as a note on the ORSA working file with the date and the two record extracts compared.
checklist.done: every ORSA operational risk scenario maps to a plan, and the risk register rating matches evidenced recovery capability.

checklist.step: Peer-review each plan against the ICP 8.3 and 16.14 content checklist
actions: Score each plan against a checklist built from ICP 8.3 and ICP 16.14: critical functions identified, recovery objectives stated, roles assigned, dependencies mapped, communication arranged, testing scheduled, review cadence set.
Reject plans whose recovery sequence is written as an aspiration ('restore service promptly') rather than as named steps with owners and elapsed-time markers.
List every checklist element failed, with the plan name and the owner, on a single remediation sheet.
Give owners 15 business days to correct, then re-score before the plan goes to committee.
checklist.done: every plan scores complete against the ICP 8.3/16.14 checklist or appears on the remediation sheet with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Take the plan set through the Board Risk Committee for annual approval
actions: Assemble the committee paper: BIA register summary, plan inventory with approval dates, RTO/RPO table with capability gaps, latest test results and the open resilience issues list.
Upload the paper to the board portal ahead of the papers deadline and table it as a decision item, not a noting item.
Present the capability gaps and the funding needed to close them, with a recommended tolerance for each unresolved gap.
Have the minute record the approval, the accepted gaps and the review date, and export the minute extract as evidence.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee minute records approval of the plan set, the accepted capability gaps and the next review date.

checklist.step: Publish the approved plans and train the named recovery teams
actions: Publish the approved plan versions to the document management repository and retire the superseded versions so only one current plan is retrievable per function.
Assign a role-based awareness module to every person named in a recovery team or call tree, with a 30-day completion deadline.
Run a walkthrough session per critical function using the plan's 24-hour recovery sequence and capture attendance.
Distribute a printed or offline copy of the call tree and invocation criteria to recovery team leads, since a network outage removes access to the repository.
Report completion rates to the Business Continuity Manager and chase anyone outstanding after 30 days.
checklist.done: current plans are the only published versions, every named recovery team member has completed training and offline call trees are distributed.

checklist.step: Keep the plans current between annual reviews on defined triggers
actions: Add a change-record question that fires whenever a change touches a tier-1 application, a critical function's process, or an outsourced provider supporting one.
Route every 'yes' answer to the plan owner as a task to refresh the affected plan section within 30 days.
Refresh the dependency map when the CMDB records a new integration or a hosting region change for a tier-1 application.
Review the call tree quarterly against the HR leaver and mover feed so no plan names someone who has left.
Report trigger-driven updates monthly to the Operational Resilience Lead.
checklist.done: plans are refreshed within 30 days of any triggering change and the call tree carries no leavers.

checklist.step: File the plan evidence for the retention period and index it for supervisors
actions: Move the approved plan versions, BIA worksheets, dependency maps, provider attestations and committee minutes into the compliance evidence repository under the review-cycle year.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label so a retired plan version survives the function it covered.
Index each record by critical function name, plan version and board approval date so an ICP 8.3 self-assessment request can be answered by search rather than by reconstruction.
Confirm with the Regulatory Affairs Manager that the index satisfies the group-wide supervisor's college pack format.
checklist.done: the plan evidence set is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable by function, version and approval date.

testing.step: Build the population of critical functions and plan versions in force
actions: Extract the full BIA register from the GRC platform as at the review date with function name, criticality, owner, RTO, RPO and last review date.
Extract the plan library listing from the document management repository with version, owner and board approval date.
Join the two extracts on function name and list every function with no plan and every plan with no BIA record.
Record the extract date, record counts and the extract query in the workpaper before any sampling.
testing.done: the population is a single joined list of critical functions and plan versions with unmatched rows already isolated.

testing.step: Reconcile the BIA register to an independent source of what the business actually does
actions: Take the CMDB list of business services flagged tier-1 and the general ledger expense lines for outsourced operational services as independent completeness sources.
Compare both to the BIA register and list any tier-1 service or material outsourced operation with no BIA record.
Ask the Business Continuity Manager to explain each difference in writing and keep the reply in the workpaper.
Treat an unexplained missing critical function as a completeness failure of the whole register, not a single-row exception.
testing.done: the BIA register reconciles to the CMDB tier-1 list and outsourced service spend, with every difference explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record how it was drawn
actions: Take 100% of functions rated highest criticality and 100% of functions whose RTO is 24 hours or less.
Take 10 further functions selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining register, for a minimum of 20 sampled functions.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector name in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every function that failed last cycle's test as a mandatory sample row regardless of the random draw.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all highest-criticality and short-RTO functions and carries forward prior-year failures.

testing.step: Re-perform the plan-completeness assessment against ICP 8.3 and 16.14
actions: Open each sampled plan from the repository and score it independently against the ICP 8.3/16.14 elements without first reading the preparer's checklist score.
Check the plan states an RTO and RPO, names a recovery team with alternates, carries a dependency map and describes a manual workaround in executable terms.
Compare your score to the recorded score; any difference, including a pass recorded on a plan with an aspirational recovery sequence, is an exception.
Capture the plan cover page and the recovery sequence section into the workpaper as the evidence relied on.
testing.done: each sampled plan has an independent completeness score with the source pages captured, and score differences are logged.

testing.step: Trace stated RTOs to evidenced recovery capability rather than to intent
actions: For each sampled function take the stated RTO and find the most recent recovery test result or real invocation for its tier-1 applications.
Compare the achieved recovery time and the measured replication lag to the stated RTO and RPO.
Where no test or invocation evidence exists in the last 12 months, record the RTO as unsubstantiated.
List every function where the stated RTO exceeds evidenced capability and quantify the shortfall in hours.
testing.done: every sampled RTO is either substantiated by dated test evidence or listed as unsubstantiated with the shortfall in hours.

testing.step: Verify board approval dates and the annual review cadence
actions: Pull the Board Risk Committee minutes from the board portal for the review cycle and locate the approval resolution for the plan set.
Check the version approved in the minute matches the version currently published for each sampled function.
Recompute the interval between the current approval date and the prior one and flag any plan whose interval exceeds 12 months.
Confirm the minute records the accepted capability gaps rather than approving the set silently.
testing.done: each sampled plan traces to a board approval within 12 months of the prior approval for the exact published version.

testing.step: Test the dependency and third-party mapping on the sample
actions: For each sampled function, pull its provider list from the plan and the provider records for that function from the contract repository.
List providers present in the contract repository but absent from the plan, and providers named in the plan with no live contract.
For three sampled providers read the contract's continuity and step-in clauses and compare the contractual recovery commitment to the function's RTO.
Flag any function relying on a provider whose contractual commitment is weaker than the RTO with no recorded substitutability option.
testing.done: provider lists in plans reconcile to live contracts and every commitment shortfall is either mitigated or logged.

testing.step: Walk the manual workaround with the people who would run it
actions: Pick three sampled functions and interview two named recovery team members each without prior notice of which function will be tested.
Ask them to locate the current plan offline, state the invocation trigger and describe the first three steps of the workaround.
Check the offline call tree in their possession against the current published version for leavers and wrong numbers.
Record failures to locate the plan or to state the trigger as an operating-effectiveness exception, distinct from a design exception.
testing.done: walkthroughs are documented per person with design and operating-effectiveness exceptions recorded separately.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception in the GRC platform with function name, the ICP element failed and the policyholder impact if the disruption occurred today.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (BIA not refreshed, dependency map stale, provider commitment gap, RTO unsubstantiated, plan not approved in cycle) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next review cycle and require the Chief Risk Officer's acceptance for any date beyond it.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's sample as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the pass rate against the threshold that every critical function holds an approved plan under 12 months old with a substantiated RTO.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, and reference the workpaper sections that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no sampled plan and sits outside business continuity and IT operations, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open issues to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository indexed by cycle year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, pass rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual resilience and disaster-recovery test programme and the test results register; escalates any tier-1 application that fails its RTO twice running to the Head of IT and the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Corrected at verification - the citation string carried on this item (ICP 22 Standard 22.3 and ICP 15 Standards 15.6-15.8) covers AML risk-based measures and derivatives, not resilience testing; the governing text is ICP 8 Standard 8.3 (business continuity, including testing) and ICP 16 Standard 16.14, re-read in the consolidated ICP text, with EU DORA Articles 24-27 (annual testing programme, three-yearly threat-led penetration testing) as the binding local transposition. The mapping correction is logged against the regulation record.

In-scope processes.value: The annual resilience test programme: tier-1 application failover and failback tests, backup restore tests, data-corruption recovery tests, third-party and intragroup service invocation tests, and the crisis-management exercise for each critical function on the BIA register

In-scope systems.value: Test change records, runbook execution tickets and defect records; timing evidence taken from Grafana dashboards and the SIEM, results register held in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Resilience Testing Standard - test types and their minimum cadence, scenario design rules, entry and exit criteria, the requirement to measure actual elapsed recovery time against RTO, defect classification and re-test rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Annual test plan approved by the Head of IT and endorsed by the Board Risk Committee alongside the plan set; scenario changes approved by the Operational Resilience Lead

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every tier-1 application tested at least once in each 12-month cycle; crisis-management exercise for each critical function annually; threat-led penetration test on the three-year cycle; results reported to the Board Risk Committee within 30 days of test completion

Deadline reminders configured.value: Test calendar entries in the ITSM platform with reminders at T-60 (scenario sign-off), T-30 (environment readiness) and T-7 (participant confirmation), plus a monthly overdue-test report to the Head of IT

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test plan, scenario, execution log with timestamps, screenshots of recovered service, defect records and the post-test report retained 7 years from the test date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed test, a test that did not measure elapsed recovery time, or an RTO/RPO breach at test is logged as a resilience defect with severity, root cause, owner and re-test date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of IT signs off closure of every severity-1 test defect and every re-test that demonstrates the RTO was met

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every tier-1 application in the CMDB and every critical function on the BIA register in the cycle, joined to the test results register for the same period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Each tier-1 application must have a completed test in the 12-month cycle with an actual elapsed recovery time recorded at or below its RTO and data loss at or below its RPO; a test with no recorded elapsed time is treated as not performed. Any tier-1 application untested or breaching RTO fails, and two consecutive failures escalate to the Board Risk Committee.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is an annual test cycle running continuously, so verification runs annually over the full cycle, with a quarterly interim check that the test calendar is on track and that severity-1 defects are being re-tested

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in IT operations or disaster recovery and must not have executed or observed any sampled test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual resilience testing workpaper (test calendar extract, results register, sampled execution logs, defect ageing, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by application and test date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Testing programme pack - annual test plan, per-test post-test reports with measured recovery times, defect register and re-test evidence - producible for a group-wide supervisor or a DORA testing-programme request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns the supervisory request; the Chief Info Security Officer clears anything describing penetration-test findings and the Chief Risk Officer clears any statement that an RTO is achievable

checklist.step: Build the annual resilience test calendar from the BIA and the CMDB
actions: Extract every application flagged tier-1 in the CMDB with its business service, hosting model and recovery architecture.
Join to the RTO/RPO register so each planned test carries the objective it must demonstrate.
Slot each application into a test month, avoiding the actuarial valuation close, the annual statement filing window and the peak renewal period agreed with the Controller and the Appointed Actuary.
Add the annual crisis-management exercise per critical function and the three-year threat-led penetration test to the same calendar.
Publish the calendar in the ITSM platform as scheduled change records with the test owner named on each.
checklist.done: every tier-1 application and critical function has a dated test slot and a named test owner in the published calendar.

checklist.step: Design the scenario for each test so it proves the objective rather than the happy path
actions: Write the scenario as a concrete failure: loss of the primary hosting region, corruption of the policy master data set, loss of the payment file transfer, or unavailability of the outsourced claims administrator.
State the measurable objective: restore the named business service within the RTO and demonstrate data loss no greater than the RPO.
Set entry criteria (backup verified, participants confirmed, rollback plan approved) and exit criteria (service transacting a real business function, not just responding to a health check).
Name what will NOT be simulated and record the residual risk that leaves, so the post-test report cannot overclaim.
Get the Operational Resilience Lead to sign the scenario 60 days before the test date.
checklist.done: each test has a signed scenario naming the failure, the measurable objective, entry and exit criteria and the unsimulated residual.

checklist.step: Prepare the test environment and the participant roster
actions: Confirm the standby region or recovery environment is provisioned from the same infrastructure code as production and record the code version used.
Verify data replication is current: capture the replication lag reading from the monitoring dashboard immediately before the test and record it as the starting RPO position.
Confirm the participant roster - platform, network, database, application support and the business validator from the owning function - and get each one's written confirmation.
Raise the change record with the rollback plan, the maintenance window and the business sign-off to proceed.
Freeze unrelated changes to the application for the test window through the Change Coordinator.
checklist.done: the recovery environment is provisioned from versioned code, replication lag is recorded and every participant has confirmed.

checklist.step: Execute the failover and start the clock
actions: Declare the test start time in the execution ticket to the minute - this timestamp is the RTO clock start and cannot be adjusted afterwards.
Execute the runbook steps in order: promote the standby database, redirect the load balancer or DNS record, restart the application tier in the recovery region, re-point the batch scheduler.
Log each step with its start and end time and note every deviation from the runbook and the reason for it.
Capture the monitoring dashboard showing service health and the SIEM entries showing traffic arriving at the recovery region.
Where a step fails, do not fix it silently - record the failure, the workaround used and the minutes lost.
checklist.done: a timestamped execution log records every runbook step, every deviation and the minutes lost to each failure.

checklist.step: Have the business validate that the recovered service actually transacts
actions: Run the agreed business validation scripts in the recovered environment - issue a test policy endorsement, register a claim and produce a payment instruction, or run a premium billing cycle, depending on the application.
Have the owning function's validator (Policy Admin Ops Lead, Claims Analyst or Billing Operations Manager) confirm in writing that the output is correct, not merely that the screen loaded.
Record the timestamp of the first successful business transaction - this, not service availability, stops the RTO clock.
Capture screenshots of the completed transaction and its identifiers into the test evidence folder.
checklist.done: a named business validator has confirmed a real transaction completed in the recovered environment, with its timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: Measure the achieved RTO and RPO against the objective
actions: Compute achieved RTO as first successful business transaction time minus declared test start time, in hours and minutes.
Compute achieved RPO from the replication lag reading at the moment of failover and confirm it against the last committed transaction identifier present in the recovered database.
Compare both figures to the register values and mark the test Pass or Fail on that comparison alone - a completed test that misses the RTO is a Fail, not a partial pass.
Paste the monitoring charts covering the test window into the results record as the timing evidence.
Enter achieved RTO, achieved RPO, pass/fail and the evidence links into the test results register in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: achieved RTO and RPO are computed from timestamps, compared to the register and recorded with a pass or fail and chart evidence.

checklist.step: Test the restore-from-backup path separately from failover
actions: Select a backup set from the retention depth required by the plan (most recent, plus one from beyond the corruption-detection window) and restore it to an isolated environment.
Run integrity checks and reconcile record counts and control totals for policy, claim and payment tables against the source-of-record as at the backup timestamp.
Record the elapsed restore time and compare it to the plan's data-corruption recovery objective.
Record the last successful restore date on the application's DR plan so the plan never claims an untested restore path.
checklist.done: a backup from within retention has been restored, reconciled on control totals and its elapsed restore time recorded.

checklist.step: Fail back and prove the production position is clean
actions: Execute the failback runbook: re-establish replication in the original direction, verify no divergence between the two copies, and return traffic to the primary region.
Reconcile transactions written during the test window so nothing is duplicated or lost, and have the owning function confirm the reconciliation.
Close the change record with the actual end time and any residual configuration left in place.
Raise a defect for any manual configuration that had to be applied by hand during failover or failback - that is a resilience gap, not housekeeping.
checklist.done: failback is complete, the transaction reconciliation is confirmed by the owning function and manual interventions are raised as defects.

checklist.step: Exercise the third-party and intragroup dependencies
actions: For each provider supporting a tested critical function, invoke the contractual continuity contact and confirm the escalation path answers within the contracted response time.
Obtain the provider's own most recent DR test attestation with test date, scope and achieved recovery times, and file it against the contract record.
Run at least one joint exercise a year with the highest-criticality provider (claims TPA, payment processor or cloud host) covering a real service interruption scenario.
Record any provider that cannot evidence a test in the last 12 months as a third-party resilience issue and feed it to the Third-Party Risk Manager.
checklist.done: each critical provider has a dated test attestation on file and one joint exercise per year is evidenced for the highest-criticality provider.

checklist.step: Run the crisis-management exercise for each critical function
actions: Run a facilitated exercise using the plan's invocation triggers, with the actual crisis-management team and no prior sight of the injects.
Inject escalating events: initial outage, confirmation of data loss, media enquiry, supervisor enquiry, and a second site affected.
Keep a decision log with times so the exercise measures decision latency, not just attendance.
Test the out-of-band call tree live by contacting three named alternates during the exercise.
Write the observations into the post-exercise report within 10 business days with named owners for each improvement.
checklist.done: each critical function has a facilitated exercise with a timed decision log, a live call-tree test and a report with owned improvements.

checklist.step: Classify and record every defect the test produced
actions: Raise one defect per finding with severity: 1 (RTO or RPO missed, or recovery not achieved), 2 (achieved but with undocumented manual intervention), 3 (documentation or contact-detail error).
Assign an owner and a fix-by date - 30 days for severity 1, 90 days for severity 2, next plan review for severity 3.
Link each defect to the application, the critical function and the plan section it affects.
Schedule the mandatory re-test for every severity-1 defect within 90 days of the fix.
checklist.done: every finding is a severity-classified defect with an owner, a fix-by date and, for severity 1, a scheduled re-test.

checklist.step: Write the post-test report and feed it back into the plans
actions: Write the report covering scenario, participants, timeline, achieved RTO/RPO against objective, defects raised and the residual risk left by anything not simulated.
Update the affected business continuity and DR plans with the corrected runbook steps, contact details and realistic recovery times within 30 days.

Where achieved recovery time is persistently worse than the stated RTO, propose either an architecture investment or a formal RTO change to the Business Continuity Manager - do not leave the plan claiming the unachievable.
Publish the report to the plan owner, the Head of IT and the Operational Resilience Lead.
checklist.done: a post-test report is published within 10 business days and the affected plans are updated within 30 days.

checklist.step: Re-test severity-1 defects and prove the fix
actions: Re-run the failed portion of the scenario against the same objective, with the same measurement rules and a fresh declared start time.
Confirm the specific defect no longer occurs and that the fix did not introduce a new manual step.
Record the re-test result in the results register linked to the original defect, and only then close the defect.
Where the re-test fails again, escalate to the Head of IT and the Chief Risk Officer the same week with the two failed measurements side by side.
checklist.done: every severity-1 defect has a linked re-test with a measured result, and second failures are escalated the same week.

checklist.step: Report the testing programme to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Report tests completed versus planned, achieved RTO/RPO against objective per tier-1 application, open severity-1 defects and their ageing.
Name explicitly every critical function whose recovery capability is not evidenced, and the exposure that leaves.
Table the funding request for any architecture change needed to close a persistent RTO shortfall.
Have the minute record the committee's acceptance of the residual position and the date it will be revisited.
checklist.done: the committee minute records completion rates, unevidenced functions and an accepted residual position with a revisit date.

checklist.step: File the test evidence for the retention period
actions: Move test plans, scenarios, timestamped execution logs, monitoring captures, business validation confirmations, defect records and post-test reports into the compliance evidence repository under the test date.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the test date.
Index each record by application, critical function, test type and achieved RTO so a supervisory request can be answered by search.
Confirm penetration-test reports are stored with restricted access and referenced, not duplicated, in the general programme pack.
checklist.done: test evidence is filed with 7-year retention, indexed by application and test type, with penetration-test reports access-restricted.

testing.step: Build the population of required tests and tests actually performed
actions: Extract every tier-1 application from the CMDB and every critical function from the BIA register as the required-test population for the cycle.
Extract the test results register from the GRC platform for the same 12-month period with application, test date, achieved RTO, achieved RPO and pass/fail.
Join the two and list every required test with no result record - untested applications are the finding most likely to be missing from the register itself.
Record extract dates, record counts and queries in the workpaper before sampling.
testing.done: a joined required-versus-performed list exists with untested applications and functions already isolated.

testing.step: Reconcile the results register to independent execution evidence
actions: Extract all change records of type Disaster Recovery Test closed in the period from the ITSM platform.
Compare that list to the results register and investigate tests executed with no register entry and register entries with no change record.
Confirm the change record's actual start and end times agree with the timestamps used to compute the achieved RTO.
Treat any register entry whose timing cannot be tied to an execution record as unsupported.
testing.done: the results register reconciles to closed DR test change records and unsupported entries are listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of tests recorded as Fail, 100% of tier-1 applications supporting claim payment or benefit disbursement, and 100% of applications with an RTO of 24 hours or less.
Take 8 further tests at random with a recorded seed from the remaining results, for a minimum of 15 sampled tests.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every severity-1 defect from the prior cycle as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all failures and short-RTO applications and carries forward prior-cycle severity-1 defects.

testing.step: Re-perform the recovery-time computation from raw timestamps
actions: For each sampled test take the declared start time from the execution ticket and the first successful business transaction timestamp from the validation evidence.
Recompute the achieved RTO independently and compare it to the register figure to the minute.
Check the clock stop used the first business transaction, not service health or login availability - a health check stop is an exception even where the total is within RTO.
Capture the monitoring chart and the transaction evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: achieved RTO is independently recomputed for every sampled test and differences or wrong clock-stop bases are logged.

testing.step: Verify the achieved RPO against actual data evidence
actions: For each sampled test read the recorded pre-failover replication lag and the last committed transaction identifier present in the recovered environment.
Compare the gap between that identifier and the last transaction in the primary at failover time to the stated achieved RPO.
Where the test recorded an RPO with no supporting transaction identifier or lag capture, record it as unsupported.
Flag any test whose achieved RPO exceeds the register RPO but was still marked Pass.
testing.done: each sampled achieved RPO is supported by a lag capture and a transaction identifier, or listed as unsupported.

testing.step: Test scenario quality and the unsimulated residual
actions: Read each sampled scenario and judge whether it forced a genuine failure or was executed as a planned, pre-warmed switchover.
Check the scenario names what was not simulated and that the residual risk statement made it into the post-test report and the plan.
Flag tests where the standby environment had been pre-scaled or pre-warmed outside the runbook, since that invalidates the measured RTO.
Confirm the scenario was signed by an owner independent of the executing engineer before the test date.
testing.done: each sampled scenario is judged for realism, its unsimulated residual is traced into the plan, and pre-warmed tests are flagged.

testing.step: Check business validation was performed by the business, not by IT
actions: For each sampled test identify the named validator and confirm they sit in the owning business function, not in the executing technology team.
Trace the validation evidence to a real transaction identifier - endorsement number, claim number or payment reference - in the recovered environment.
Confirm the validator's written confirmation is dated on the test date, not backfilled afterwards.
Record IT self-validation as an exception regardless of whether the RTO was met.
testing.done: each sampled test shows same-day written validation by a named business validator tied to a real transaction identifier.

testing.step: Age the defect population and test re-test discipline
actions: Extract all test defects raised in the cycle with severity, raise date, fix-by date and closure date, and compute ageing at the review date.
Check every severity-1 defect closed in the period has a linked re-test record with a measured result, not just a fix note.
Recompute the fix-by dates against the standard (30 days severity 1, 90 days severity 2) and list defects closed after their due date or with the date extended without Head of IT approval.
List any severity-1 defect closed with no re-test as a control failure.
testing.done: defect ageing is computed, every closed severity-1 defect has a measured re-test and late or unapproved extensions are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with application, critical function, the element failed and the policyholder impact implied.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (test not scheduled, scenario not realistic, timing not measured, business validation absent, defect not re-tested) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and require Head of IT acceptance for any date beyond the next cycle's test slot for that application.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's sample as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the completion rate (tests performed over tests required) and the RTO achievement rate across the cycle.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who executed and observed none of the sampled tests and sits outside IT operations, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting, name the applications whose recovery capability remains unevidenced, and file the signed workpaper indexed by cycle year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completion and RTO achievement rates, names unevidenced applications and records the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the critical third-party and ICT provider register required by the ERM framework under ICP 16.1; escalates any critical provider operating without a completed risk assessment to the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - ICP 16 Standards 16.1 and 16.3 (ERM framework covering all reasonably foreseeable and relevant material risks, including outsourcing) and ICP 8 Standard 8.6 (outsourcing of material activities) re-read in the consolidated ICP text, then traced to the binding local rules: EU DORA Articles 28-30 and the Article 28(3) Register of Information, PRA SS2/21 outsourcing and third-party risk, and EIOPA Guidelines on outsourcing to cloud service providers

In-scope processes.value: Third-party lifecycle for providers touching a critical function: intake and criticality tiering, pre-contract due diligence, contract clause coverage, onboarding to the register, ongoing monitoring, concentration and subcontractor (nth-party) mapping, and exit

In-scope systems.value: Contract records, clause coverage flags and renewal dates as the source of contractual truth; register of information maintained in the GRC platform and reconciled to procurement spend in Coupa / SAP Ariba

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third-Party and ICT Risk Management Procedure - criticality tiering rules, minimum due-diligence pack by tier, mandatory contract clauses (audit and access, sub-outsourcing consent, data location, service levels, step-in, exit assistance, incident notification), register data standard and monitoring cadence by tier

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Info Security Officer; register data standard re-approved whenever the supervisory reporting template changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register maintained continuously with a new arrangement recorded within 10 business days of contract signature; full register attestation each quarter; annual submission of the register of information to the competent authority on the supervisor's template (DORA reporting window closing 30 April); prior notification to the supervisor before entering a material outsourcing

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow alerts at contract signature, at T-90 to each critical contract renewal or expiry, at T-60 to the annual register submission date, and monthly to any register record missing a mandatory field

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register versions, due-diligence packs, clause-coverage assessments, monitoring reports, subcontractor notifications and exit plans retained 7 years from termination of the arrangement

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A critical arrangement absent from the register, a register record with missing mandatory fields, a missing mandatory contract clause or an overdue monitoring review is logged as a third-party risk issue with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs off every critical arrangement allowed to continue with a missing mandatory clause and every register completeness failure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All live third-party arrangements in the register at the review date, joined to the contract repository and to accounts-payable vendor spend for the year so unregistered providers surface

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every provider supporting a critical function must appear in the register with all mandatory fields populated, a due-diligence pack under 12 months old, full mandatory-clause coverage and an exit plan; any missing element fails. A critical provider with no register record at all is a reportable control failure, not an exception.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so completeness testing runs quarterly on new and changed arrangements and in full annually ahead of the register submission to the competent authority

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside procurement, vendor management and third-party risk and must not have performed any sampled due diligence

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual third-party register workpapers (register extract, AP spend reconciliation, sample, clause testing, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by provider and review period

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Register of information in the supervisor's template plus the contract, due-diligence and monitoring evidence for any provider queried, producible within 10 business days of a supervisory request or an outsourcing thematic review

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager submits the register to the competent authority and owns follow-up queries; General Counsel clears any disclosure of contract terms or provider names outside the register template

checklist.step: Sweep procurement and payables for every live third-party arrangement
actions: Extract from the procurement system every supplier with an active contract or a purchase order raised in the last 24 months, with spend, category and requesting cost centre.
Extract the same period's vendor payments from the general ledger with the Accounts Payable Specialist so providers paid outside a purchase order are captured.
Strip out non-service suppliers (utilities, office consumables) using the category code, and keep everything that processes data, hosts a system, or performs a business activity.
Hand the resulting candidate list, with spend and cost centre, to the Third-Party Risk Manager for tiering.
Record the extract dates and totals so the sweep can be reproduced.
checklist.done: a reproducible candidate list of every service and ICT provider exists, reconciled to procurement contracts and vendor payments.

checklist.step: Tier each arrangement by criticality against the critical-function map
actions: For each candidate, ask the business owner which critical function on the BIA register it supports and whether the function could run without it for the function's RTO.
Apply the tiering rules: Critical (supports a critical function, or holds policyholder personal data at scale, or cannot be substituted inside the RTO), Important, Standard.
Record the tiering rationale in one sentence naming the function and the substitution position - not just a tier letter.
Have the business owner and the Operational Resilience Lead countersign every Critical tiering so the tier cannot be quietly downgraded to avoid the due-diligence pack.
Set the monitoring cadence from the tier: Critical quarterly, Important semi-annual, Standard annual.
checklist.done: every arrangement carries a tier, a one-sentence rationale naming the supported function and a countersignature on Critical tierings.

checklist.step: Complete the due-diligence pack before contract or renewal for every Critical provider
actions: Collect the tier-mandated pack: latest audited financial statements, SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate with scope and dates, penetration-test summary, business continuity and DR test attestation, insurance certificates, sanctions and adverse-media screening on the entity and its owners.
Read the SOC 2 scope section and confirm it actually covers the service being bought and the hosting locations used, and read the exceptions section rather than the opinion page alone.
Record every certificate's expiry date in the register so lapse is detected before renewal, not at audit.
Where a pack element is missing, record the compensating control and the risk acceptance rather than marking the pack complete.
File the pack against the provider record and set its next refresh date at 12 months.
checklist.done: each Critical provider has a dated pack with scope-checked assurance reports, recorded certificate expiries and named gaps with compensating controls.

checklist.step: Assess the security and data position of every ICT arrangement
actions: Record the data classification processed, the data locations (country of storage and of processing, including support access from other countries) and the lawful transfer mechanism confirmed with the Data Protection Officer.
Record the access model: who at the provider can reach production data, whether privileged access is brokered through the company's PAM, and how access is revoked at exit.
Record the integration surface - APIs, file transfers, VPN or direct connections - and confirm each is inventoried in the CMDB.
Record the provider's incident notification commitment in hours and check it is short enough to meet the company's own supervisory reporting deadlines under REG-013-C52.
Route any provider with production data access and no brokered privileged access to the Chief Info Security Officer for decision.
checklist.done: each ICT arrangement records data classification, locations, transfer basis, access model, integration surface and a notification commitment that fits the reporting deadlines.

checklist.step: Test the contract against the mandatory clause set
actions: Open the executed contract in the contract repository and mark each mandatory clause present or absent: audit and access rights for the company and its supervisors, sub-outsourcing consent and notification, data location and transfer, service levels with remedies, security requirements, incident notification within a stated number of hours, step-in, termination rights, and exit assistance with data return format.
Quote the clause reference and the operative sentence into the clause-coverage record - a tick with no reference is not evidence.
List every absent clause for a Critical provider and open a contract-variation request with the provider through Legal Counsel.
Set the register field 'supervisor access rights' from the contract text, since that is a field the supervisory template demands.
Flag contracts governed by a law that would frustrate supervisory access to the General Counsel.
checklist.done: each Critical contract has a clause-coverage record quoting the operative sentence per mandatory clause, with absences raised as variation requests.

checklist.step: Create or update the register record to the supervisory data standard
actions: Within 10 business days of signature, create the register record with the mandatory fields: legal entity name and identifier, corporate group, country of registration, contract start and end dates, notice period, function supported, criticality tier, data locations, annual cost, governing law and supervisor access rights.
Populate the intragroup flag and the entity within the insurance group that is the contracting party, so group-level concentration can be seen.
Reject any record submitted with a blank mandatory field rather than saving a partial row - partial rows are what break the annual submission.
Link the record to the contract in the contract repository and to the supported critical function on the BIA register.
checklist.done: every new arrangement has a complete register record within 10 business days of signature, linked to its contract and supported function.

checklist.step: Map subcontractors and the nth-party chain for Critical providers
actions: Require each Critical provider to disclose in writing every subcontractor performing a material part of the service, with the function performed and the country.
Record the chain to the level where the service actually runs - name the underlying cloud provider and region behind a SaaS platform rather than stopping at the contracting party.
Check the disclosure against the contract's sub-outsourcing consent clause and challenge any subcontractor added without the required notice.
Update the register's subcontractor fields and re-run the concentration analysis whenever a disclosure changes.
checklist.done: each Critical provider's chain is recorded down to the operating cloud provider and region, with unnotified subcontractors challenged.

checklist.step: Run the concentration analysis across providers, groups and regions
actions: Aggregate the register by corporate group, by underlying cloud provider and by hosting region, and count the critical functions each one supports.
Identify single points of failure - one provider group behind several critical functions, or several providers all hosted in the same region.
Compute the substitutability position for each concentration: named alternate provider, in-house fallback, or none, with the time to switch.
Present concentrations with no substitution option to the Board Risk Committee alongside the resilience plan set, not as a separate procurement matter.
checklist.done: concentration by group, cloud provider and region is quantified, with a substitution position and switch time for each concentration.

checklist.step: Write and keep current an exit plan for every Critical arrangement
actions: Document the exit scenario for both planned termination and provider failure: the alternate provider or in-house route, the data return format and schedule from the contract, and the estimated elapsed time to transition.
Confirm the data return clause specifies a usable format and a deletion certificate, and that the company holds a current copy or export of the data it would need.
Cost the exit and record it, so the risk acceptance is made with the switching cost visible.
Have the supported function's business owner confirm the exit route is operationally credible within the function's RTO.
Review the exit plan at each contract renewal and after any change in the provider's subcontractor chain.
checklist.done: each Critical arrangement has a costed exit plan with a data return route confirmed as credible by the business owner.

checklist.step: Run the tier-based monitoring cycle and record the outcome
actions: For Critical providers, hold a quarterly service review with the provider covering service levels achieved, incidents raised, open remediation actions and any change in subcontractors or locations.
Refresh the assurance evidence when a certificate expires - request the new SOC 2 or ISO certificate before the recorded expiry date rather than after.
Re-screen the provider entity and its beneficial owners against sanctions and adverse media, and route any hit to the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Record the review outcome, the actions and the next review date on the register record; an unheld review is an overdue item, not a silent skip.
checklist.done: each Critical provider has a dated quarterly review with service levels, incidents, re-screening and a next review date recorded.

checklist.step: Notify the supervisor before entering or materially changing a material outsourcing
actions: Determine, with Regulatory Counsel, whether the arrangement is a material outsourcing under each relevant supervisor's rules and record the determination and its basis.

Where notification is required, prepare the notification setting out the function outsourced, the provider, the locations, the risk assessment summary and the exit arrangements, and send it before the arrangement takes effect.
Log the notification date, the supervisor, the channel used and any acknowledgement or objection on the arrangement's register record.
Repeat for material changes: change of provider group, change of hosting country or addition of a material subcontractor.
checklist.done: every material outsourcing carries a dated pre-effective notification with the supervisor's acknowledgement logged on the register record.

checklist.step: Attest the register quarterly with the business owners
actions: Issue each business owner their slice of the register and ask them to confirm the providers listed are the ones actually used, the tier is right, and no provider is missing.
Require a positive statement naming any provider used but not listed - a silent return counts as not completed.
Chase non-returns at 10 and 15 business days and escalate outstanding owners to their function head at 20.
Record the attestation date, the attestor and any additions on the register version for the quarter.
checklist.done: each quarter closes with a dated positive attestation per business owner and any newly disclosed providers added to the register.

checklist.step: Submit the register of information to the competent authority on its template
actions: Export the register into the supervisor's reporting template and run the template's validation rules before submission.
Resolve validation failures at source in the register rather than by editing the export, so the register and the submission stay identical.
Reconcile record counts and total annual cost between the register and the submitted file, and record the reconciliation in the submission pack.
Submit through the supervisor's collection channel ahead of the annual deadline (30 April under the DORA reporting window) and file the submission receipt.
Store the exact file submitted with its validation report so the submission can be reproduced on request.
checklist.done: the register is submitted ahead of the annual deadline with a validation report, a count and cost reconciliation and a filed receipt.

checklist.step: Close arrangements out of the register at termination
actions: On termination, record the end date, the exit route actually used and the date the data return and deletion certificate were received.
Confirm with the IAM Engineer that all provider accounts, API keys and network connections were revoked, and record the revocation date.
Confirm with the business owner that the function is now served by the alternate route and that no residual dependency remains.
Set the record to Terminated rather than deleting it, and apply the 7-year retention from the termination date.
checklist.done: terminated arrangements show an end date, evidenced data return and deletion, revoked access and a retained record.

checklist.step: Report the third-party risk position to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Report register completeness, Critical providers with overdue due diligence or reviews, missing mandatory clauses, and the concentration positions with no substitution option.
Name the supported critical functions behind each concentration so the committee sees the policyholder exposure, not a supplier count.
Table any risk acceptance requested for a Critical provider operating without a mandatory clause, with the compensating control.
Have the minute record the accepted positions and the review date.
checklist.done: the committee minute records register completeness, concentration exposures and each accepted position with a review date.

testing.step: Build the population of live arrangements from the register
actions: Extract the full register at the review date with provider, entity identifier, tier, supported function, contract dates, data locations, annual cost and last review date.
Split the extract by tier and note the count of Critical arrangements as the primary test population.
Record the extract date, counts and query in the workpaper before sampling.
List register records with any blank mandatory field as automatic exceptions before any judgement is applied.
testing.done: the register population is extracted by tier with blank-mandatory-field records already isolated as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to spend and to the contract repository for completeness
actions: Extract vendor payments for the year from the general ledger above a stated threshold and match them to register records on vendor name and legal entity identifier.
Extract active contracts from the contract repository and match them to register records the same way.
Investigate every paid vendor or live contract with no register record and ask the business owner what function it supports.
Treat any unregistered provider supporting a critical function as a register completeness failure covering the whole register, not a single-row exception.
testing.done: the register reconciles to vendor spend and live contracts, and any unregistered critical provider is raised as a completeness failure.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of Critical arrangements, 100% of arrangements onboarded or materially changed in the period, and 100% of intragroup arrangements supporting a critical function.
Take 15 further arrangements at random with a recorded seed from the Important and Standard tiers.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every provider with an open third-party risk issue from the prior period as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all Critical, new and intragroup arrangements and carries forward open issues.

testing.step: Re-perform the criticality tiering independently
actions: For each sampled arrangement read the supported function on the BIA register and reach your own tier conclusion before reading the recorded tier.
Test the substitution assertion: ask the business owner what happens on day one without the provider and compare the answer to the recorded rationale.
Flag every downgrade from Critical whose rationale does not survive that question, since a downgrade removes the due-diligence and exit obligations.
Record the independent tier, the recorded tier and the difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled arrangement has an independent tier conclusion, and unsupported downgrades from Critical are logged.

testing.step: Test the due-diligence pack for currency and scope
actions: For each sampled Critical provider open the assurance reports and check the report period ends within the last 12 months and the certificate has not expired.
Read the SOC 2 or ISO scope statement and confirm it names the service and the hosting locations the company actually uses.
Read the exceptions or qualifications section and check each one was assessed, not ignored, in the provider record.
Record a pack as failed where the certificate covers a different service line or a different region from the one in use, even if it is in date.
testing.done: each sampled Critical pack is tested for currency, scope match to the service used and treatment of report exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the contract clause coverage test
actions: Open each sampled executed contract and independently search for the mandatory clauses: audit and supervisor access, sub-outsourcing, data location, service levels, incident notification hours, step-in, termination and exit assistance.
Compare your finding to the recorded clause-coverage record, treating a recorded 'present' with no quoted operative sentence as unsupported.
Check the incident notification hours in the contract are short enough for the company to meet its own supervisory deadline under REG-013-C52 and flag any that are not.
Confirm any absent clause on a Critical contract has an open variation request or a CRO risk acceptance dated before the review date.
testing.done: clause coverage is independently re-performed per sampled contract, with unsupported ticks and unmitigated gaps listed.

testing.step: Trace the subcontractor chain and test the concentration analysis
actions: For five sampled Critical providers request the current subcontractor disclosure and compare it to the register's subcontractor fields.
Confirm the chain resolves to the operating cloud provider and region rather than stopping at the contracting party.
Recompute the concentration counts by corporate group, cloud provider and region from the raw register extract and compare to the reported figures.
Flag any concentration reported to the committee that understates the count once the chain is resolved.
testing.done: subcontractor chains reconcile to provider disclosures and concentration figures are independently recomputed from the raw register.

testing.step: Test exit plans and monitoring cadence on the sample
actions: For each sampled Critical arrangement confirm an exit plan exists, names a specific alternate route and carries a costed transition time confirmed by the business owner.
Recompute the monitoring due dates from the tier cadence and the last review date, and list every review overdue at the review date with days overdue.
Check certificate expiry dates in the register against the actual certificates and list any lapse that went undetected.
Treat an exit plan whose alternate route is 'bring in-house' with no named capacity or cost as no exit plan.
testing.done: each sampled Critical arrangement has a credible costed exit plan, and overdue reviews and lapsed certificates are listed with ageing.

testing.step: Test the annual submission against the register it came from
actions: Retrieve the exact file submitted to the competent authority, its validation report and the submission receipt with its date.
Reconcile record counts, entity identifiers and total annual cost between the submitted file and the register extract as at the submission date.
Confirm the submission date is on or before the annual deadline and that any validation failure was fixed in the register rather than only in the export.
List any field in the submitted file that differs from the register as a data-integrity exception.
testing.done: the submitted file reconciles to the register on counts, identifiers and cost, and was filed on or before the deadline.

testing.step: Log exceptions, obtain independent sign-off and conclude
actions: Raise one issue per exception with provider, tier, the element failed and the critical function exposed, and assign a root cause from a fixed list (not registered, tiering unsupported, due diligence stale, clause missing, review overdue, exit plan absent, submission mismatch) with an owner and a remediation date.
Compute the register completeness rate and the Critical-provider compliance rate against the zero-tolerance completeness threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the workpaper references behind each rate.

Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside procurement, vendor management and third-party risk and performed none of the sampled due diligence, sign the workpaper, then report to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper indexed by review period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completeness and compliance rates, every exception carries a root cause and owner, and the committee reporting date is recorded.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the major operational and ICT incident notification decision and the clock that starts at classification; escalates any missed notification deadline to the Chief Risk Officer the same day

Citation verified against current regula.value: Corrected at verification - the citation carried on this item (ICP 22.3, ICP 15.6-15.8) covers AML and investment standards; the governing text for incident reporting is ICP 8 Standard 8.3 and ICP 16 Standard 16.14 read with ICP 25 (supervisory cooperation) on cross-border notification. The binding deadlines come from the local transpositions: EU DORA Article 19 (initial notification within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours from detection, intermediate within 72 hours, final within 1 month), NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.17(a) and the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law (72 hours), OSFI technology and cyber incident reporting (24 hours), MAS Notice 127 (1 hour). Mapping correction logged on the regulation record.

In-scope processes.value: Incident lifecycle for operational and ICT events affecting a critical function: detection, triage, severity classification, major-incident declaration, per-jurisdiction notification decision, initial/intermediate/final regulator reporting, policyholder notification, and post-incident review

Deadlines computed in the supervisor's local time from the recorded detection timestamp.

Classification accuracy threshold: no more than one downgrade in the sample overturned on re-performance, and any overturned downgrade that avoided a notification is a reportable breach.
