checklist.step: Capture the detection timestamp the moment an event is raised
actions: When an alert fires or a business report arrives, open the incident record and set the detection timestamp to the earliest moment anyone in the firm knew - the alert time in the SIEM, not the time the ticket was typed.
Attach the triggering alert identifier, the detecting control and the raw log excerpt so the timestamp can be defended later.
Where the event came from a provider or a customer complaint, record the time the notification was received and from whom.
Never let a record carry a detection time later than its own first log entry - the notification clocks run from this field.
checklist.done: the incident record carries a defensible detection timestamp tied to an alert identifier or an inbound notification.

checklist.step: Triage the event against critical functions and policyholder impact
actions: Identify from the CMDB which business services and critical functions the affected components support.
Establish the four facts every supervisor asks for: is a critical function unavailable, is policyholder personal data affected, is a payment or benefit flow affected, and is the cause malicious.
Record the number of policyholders and the geographies affected, even as an estimate with a stated basis, since materiality thresholds are counted this way.
Assign the initial severity and page the duty Operational Risk Manager for any event touching a critical function, personal data or payments.
checklist.done: triage records the affected critical functions, the policyholder and geography counts, the payment impact and the malicious/non-malicious call.

checklist.step: Classify against each supervisor's materiality thresholds and stamp the classification time
actions: Open the classification worksheet and score the event against the criteria set: clients affected, duration and service downtime, geographical spread, data losses, criticality of services affected, and economic impact.
Reach a Major / Not Major decision per applicable supervisor, since the thresholds differ, and write the reasoning against each criterion rather than a bare conclusion.
Stamp the classification timestamp at the moment the decision is made - this starts the 4-hour DORA initial-notification clock while the 24-hour clock already runs from detection.
Where the facts are still moving, classify on the information available and re-classify later; delaying classification to gather facts does not stop the detection clock.
Route a Not Major decision on any event touching policyholder data or a payment flow to Regulatory Counsel for concurrence before it is closed.
checklist.done: a per-supervisor Major/Not Major decision is recorded with criterion-by-criterion reasoning and a classification timestamp.

checklist.step: Determine the jurisdictions in play and compute each deadline
actions: List every supervisor with a claim on the event: the group-wide supervisor, each legal entity's home supervisor, and any state or data-protection authority triggered by residency of the affected policyholders.

For each, read the current notification rule from the regulatory obligations register and record the deadline basis (from detection, from classification, or from becoming aware) and the hours allowed.
Compute each due date and time in the supervisor's local time from the recorded timestamps and write it onto the incident record - do not leave deadlines as a rule of thumb in someone's head.
Create one notification task per jurisdiction with its own countdown so a missed jurisdiction is visible rather than assumed covered.
checklist.done: every applicable supervisor has a named rule, a computed due date and time in local time, and its own tracked notification task.

checklist.step: Declare the major incident and stand up the crisis bridge
actions: Declare the major incident in the ITSM platform, which invokes the crisis management team through the call tree held in the business continuity plan.
Name the incident commander, the regulatory notification owner, the technical lead and the scribe, and record the names on the incident record.
Set the bridge cadence at 2-hourly for the first 12 hours and require the scribe to keep a timestamped decision log.
Instruct that no external statement, to a supervisor or a policyholder, leaves the bridge without Regulatory Counsel clearance.
checklist.done: the incident is formally declared with a named commander, notification owner and scribe, and a timestamped decision log running.

checklist.step: Draft and file the initial notification inside the shortest deadline
actions: Populate the supervisor's initial notification template: incident reference, detection and classification timestamps, description, critical functions affected, clients and geographies affected, whether malicious, current status and the contact point.
Fill unknown fields with 'not yet determined, expected by <date/time>' rather than delaying the filing - the deadline binds even where facts are incomplete.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording, then submit through each supervisor's collection channel and capture the submission receipt or reference number.
Record the actual submission time against the computed deadline on the incident record and mark the task complete only when the receipt is attached.
Notify the group-wide supervisor in parallel where the event affects more than one entity in the group.
checklist.done: each applicable supervisor has an initial notification filed before its deadline with a receipt attached to the incident record.

checklist.step: Notify affected policyholders and distributors where the trigger is met
actions: Assess whether the personal data affected triggers individual notification under the applicable privacy law and record the assessment and its basis.
Where notification is required, agree the content with Regulatory Counsel: what happened, what data, what the firm is doing, what the individual should do, and the contact route.
Give the Contact Center Ops Manager the script, the expected volume and the escalation path before the notice goes out, so the phones are staffed.
Notify affected brokers and agents through the broker portal so distributors do not learn from policyholders.
Log the notification population, the send date and the channel as evidence.
checklist.done: the individual notification assessment is recorded, and where triggered the notices are sent with population, date and channel logged.

checklist.step: Contain, recover and record the timeline as it happens
actions: Preserve forensic evidence before remediation - capture memory and disk images, export the relevant SIEM log range and place a legal hold through the General Counsel.
Execute containment (isolate hosts, revoke credentials and tokens, block indicators) and record each action with its time.
Coordinate recovery with the Disaster Recovery Manager where the business continuity plan has been invoked, so the same timeline serves both.
Record the restoration time of each affected critical function, since supervisors ask for downtime per service, not per system.
checklist.done: evidence is preserved under legal hold and the timeline records containment, recovery and per-function restoration times.

checklist.step: File the intermediate report at 72 hours with the corrected facts
actions: Update the report template with the confirmed classification figures: clients affected, downtime per critical function, data records affected, economic impact estimate and the current status of recovery.
Explicitly correct any figure supplied in the initial notification that has changed, and say so, rather than silently restating.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear it and submit before the 72-hour mark computed from the recorded basis, capturing the receipt.
Where the incident is still open at 72 hours, state the expected recovery date and the next update commitment.
checklist.done: the intermediate report is filed before its deadline with corrections to the initial figures called out explicitly and a receipt captured.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and identify root cause
actions: Hold the review within 15 business days of closure with the incident commander, the technical lead, the affected business owner and the notification owner.
Establish the root cause to a level that can be fixed - name the control that failed, not the symptom - and separate detection failures from response failures.
Measure the actual timings against the targets: detection to triage, triage to classification, classification to notification, and detection to service restoration.
Raise actions with owners and dates, including any change needed to the business continuity or DR plan and to the notification decision tree.
Feed provider-caused incidents to the Third-Party Risk Manager for the provider's register record and next service review.
checklist.done: a post-incident review within 15 business days records a fixable root cause, measured timings and owned actions.

checklist.step: File the final report within one month
actions: Assemble the final report: confirmed root cause, full timeline, total downtime per critical function, final client and data counts, direct and indirect costs, remediation completed and remediation still open with dates.
Reconcile the client and record counts to the source extracts used, so the final figures can be traced if the supervisor asks.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear it and submit within one month of the incident (or the jurisdiction's own final-report deadline) and attach the receipt.
Close the notification tasks only once every applicable jurisdiction has a filed final report or a recorded rule that none is required.
checklist.done: a final report with confirmed root cause, timeline and reconciled counts is filed within the deadline for every applicable jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Handle supervisor follow-up questions and any on-site request
actions: Log every supervisor question with its due date on the incident record and assign a single response owner.

Draft responses from the evidence already filed rather than from recollection, and keep the answer consistent with the filed reports - inconsistency is what turns an incident into an enforcement matter.
Clear technical detail with the Chief Info Security Officer before release and redact indicators that would expose other firms or ongoing investigations only with a stated basis.
File every response with its date and the supervisor's acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every supervisor question has a logged due date, a single owner and a filed response consistent with the reports already submitted.

checklist.step: Review the notification decision tree against rule changes
actions: Monitor the regulatory obligations register for changes to incident thresholds and deadlines in every jurisdiction the group writes business in.
Update the decision tree and the computed-deadline logic within 30 days of a rule change, and re-approve with the Chief Risk Officer, the Chief Info Security Officer and the General Counsel.
Re-brief the duty roster on the change and record the briefing in the learning management system.
Run a desktop test of the updated tree against the last three closed incidents to confirm it still yields the right jurisdictions.
checklist.done: the decision tree is updated and re-approved within 30 days of any rule change and back-tested against three closed incidents.

checklist.step: Rehearse the notification path so the deadline is met out of hours
actions: Run a no-notice out-of-hours exercise at least annually where the duty roster must classify a scenario and produce a draft initial notification inside the 4-hour window.
Measure detection-to-classification and classification-to-draft times and compare them to the deadlines.
Test that the duty officer can reach Regulatory Counsel and the submission channel credentials outside business hours.
Record the exercise, the measured times and the failures, and feed them into the procedure as actions.
checklist.done: an annual out-of-hours exercise evidences that a draft initial notification can be produced inside the shortest deadline.

checklist.step: File the incident evidence set for the retention period
actions: Move the incident record export, classification worksheet, jurisdiction decision, filed reports and receipts, policyholder notices and post-incident review into the compliance evidence repository under the incident number.
Apply the 7-year retention label from incident closure and confirm forensic images are retained under the separate legal-hold policy.
Index by incident number, date, critical functions affected and jurisdictions notified so a supervisory follow-up can be answered by search.
Confirm no notification receipt is missing before the record is marked complete.
checklist.done: each incident's evidence set is filed under its incident number with every notification receipt present and 7-year retention applied.

testing.step: Build the incident population for the quarter
actions: Extract every incident record opened or closed in the quarter with severity, detection timestamp, classification timestamp, affected services and notification flags.
Filter to severity 1 and 2 plus every incident of any severity touching a critical function, policyholder personal data or a payment flow.
Record the extract date, filter logic and record counts in the workpaper before sampling.
List incidents with a blank classification timestamp as automatic exceptions - the clock cannot be evidenced without it.
testing.done: the quarter's notifiable-candidate population is extracted with missing classification timestamps already isolated.

testing.step: Reconcile the incident population to independent detection sources
actions: Extract high-severity SIEM alerts, major change failures from the change record set, and complaint volume spikes from the complaints system for the same quarter.
Match each independent signal to an incident record and investigate signals with no incident, since suppressed incidents never reach classification.
Compare the SIEM alert time to the incident record's detection timestamp and list every record where detection was stamped later than the alert.
Treat a critical-function outage visible in monitoring with no incident record as a population completeness failure.
testing.done: the population reconciles to SIEM alerts, failed changes and complaint spikes, and back-dated or late detection stamps are listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of severity-1 incidents, 100% of incidents where notification was considered and declined, and 100% of incidents involving policyholder personal data.
Take 10 further incidents at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every incident with an open notification-related issue from the prior quarter as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all severity-1, declined-notification and personal-data incidents.

testing.step: Re-perform the classification against the supervisors' thresholds
actions: For each sampled incident read the underlying facts - affected services, client counts, downtime, data records, malicious or not - before reading the recorded classification.
Score the criteria independently against each applicable supervisor's threshold and reach your own Major/Not Major call.
Compare to the recorded decision; any difference is an exception, and a difference that avoided a notification is a reportable breach.
Capture the classification worksheet and the facts relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independent classification, and downgrades that avoided a notification are escalated as breaches.

testing.step: Recompute every notification deadline from the raw timestamps
actions: For each sampled notified incident recompute the due date and time per jurisdiction from the detection and classification timestamps using that jurisdiction's own basis and hours.
Convert to the supervisor's local time and compare to the actual submission timestamp on the receipt.
Compute the margin in hours and minutes for each filing and list every filing outside its deadline, however small the overrun.
Recompute the shortest applicable deadline across jurisdictions and confirm the firm worked to that one, not to the most generous.
testing.done: each notification's deadline is independently recomputed in local time and compared to the receipt timestamp with the margin recorded.

testing.step: Trace every filing to a receipt and to the correct supervisor
actions: Open the filed initial, intermediate and final reports for each sampled incident and confirm each carries a submission receipt or reference number from the supervisor's channel.
Confirm the filing went to every supervisor the decision tree required, including the group-wide supervisor where more than one entity was affected.
Check that data reported - client counts, downtime, records affected - matches the incident record's own figures.
Treat a report present in a drafts folder with no receipt as not filed.
testing.done: every required report for every required supervisor traces to a receipt with figures matching the incident record.

testing.step: Test the jurisdiction determination for completeness
actions: For each sampled incident independently list the supervisors with a claim, working from the affected legal entities and the residency of affected policyholders rather than from the recorded list.
Compare to the jurisdictions actually notified and list any supervisor missed.
Confirm the rule cited for each jurisdiction is the version in force on the incident date, not a superseded threshold.
Treat a missed jurisdiction as a breach requiring a self-report assessment, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: the jurisdiction list is independently rebuilt per sampled incident and any missed supervisor triggers a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Test declined notifications and the counsel concurrence behind them
actions: Pull every sampled incident where notification was considered and declined and read the recorded reasoning against each threshold criterion.
Confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel or General Counsel concurrence exists and pre-dates the point the deadline would have expired.
Test the underlying facts behind the decline - particularly client counts and downtime - against the source extracts rather than accepting the stated figures.
Treat a decline supported only by 'below threshold' with no criterion scoring as a fail.
testing.done: every declined notification is supported by criterion-level scoring, verified facts and a dated counsel concurrence.

testing.step: Test post-incident review completion and action closure
actions: For each sampled incident confirm a post-incident review was held within 15 business days of closure and that it names a fixable root cause rather than a symptom.
Extract the actions raised with owners and due dates, compute ageing at the review date and list overdue actions.
Confirm actions that change the notification decision tree or a continuity plan were actually applied to those documents.
Check provider-caused incidents were fed to the third-party register record for that provider.
testing.done: every sampled incident has a timely review with a fixable root cause, and action ageing and document updates are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions, obtain independent sign-off and conclude
actions: Raise one issue per exception with incident number, jurisdiction, deadline missed or classification overturned, and assign a root cause from a fixed list (detection stamped late, classification delayed, jurisdiction missed, counsel clearance bottleneck, out-of-hours cover failure) with an owner and remediation date.
Compute the on-time notification rate and the classification agreement rate against the zero-tolerance deadline threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the recomputation workpapers behind each rate.

Have the independent reviewer, who handled none of the sampled incidents and sits outside operational risk and security operations, sign the workpaper; report breaches to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper indexed by quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time notification and classification agreement rates, with every breach owned and reported to the committee.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - each determination cites the specific ICP and Standard number from the consolidated IAIS Insurance Core Principles text on iaisweb.org (this item's own carried citations are ICP 22 Standard 22.3 and ICP 15 Standards 15.6-15.8), and records that the ICPs bind supervisors rather than insurers directly, so the determination must name the local instrument through which the standard actually binds each licensed entity (for example the PRA Rulebook, Solvency II delegated acts, BMA Insurance Code of Conduct, or a state insurance code)

In-scope processes.value: Regulatory change intake for IAIS output: reading each ICP and its Standards and Guidance, testing applicability against every licensed entity and line of business (ALL and Life & Annuity), writing the determination memo, and assigning a named accountable owner with an accepted control

In-scope systems.value: Regulatory obligations register holding one record per ICP standard with applicability, local transposition, owner, control reference and review date; determination memos filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Obligation Determination Procedure - source monitoring, applicability test (entity, licence, line of business, activity performed), transposition mapping, materiality rating, owner assignment and acceptance rules, and the standing rule that no standard is closed as 'not applicable' without a named reason and counsel concurrence

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and reviewed annually and on every IAIS revision to the ICPs or ComFrame material

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Determination memo completed within 30 business days of an IAIS publication or revision; owner acceptance within a further 10 business days; full re-determination of the ICP set annually ahead of the group-wide supervisor's self-assessment cycle and whenever a new licence or entity is added

Deadline reminders configured.value: Obligations register workflow raises a determination task on publication with reminders at day 10, day 20 and day 28, and an unaccepted-owner report to the Head of Compliance every Monday

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: An ICP standard with no determination, a determination past its deadline, or an applicable standard with no accepted owner is logged as a compliance framework gap with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every 'not applicable' determination and every standard left without an accepted owner beyond the deadline

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ICP and Standard in the current consolidated ICP set, times each licensed entity in the group, as held in the obligations register at the review date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every ICP standard must carry a dated determination, a named local transposition where applicable, and a named owner who has accepted in writing; any standard with no determination fails. Any 'not applicable' call without a stated reason and counsel concurrence fails regardless of whether the conclusion is right.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per item and continuous, so the test runs quarterly over determinations made that quarter and annually across the full ICP set before the self-assessment cycle

Evidence location for test results.value: Determination coverage workpaper (register extract, ICP set reconciliation, sample, re-performance notes, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by ICP number and review period

Regulator-ready documentation.value: ICP self-assessment matrix - one row per ICP standard showing applicability, the local instrument, the owner, the control and the evidence reference - producible for the group-wide supervisor, a supervisory college or an IMF FSAP request within 10 business days
