checklist.step: Monitor IAIS output and open a determination record for each change
actions: Subscribe to the IAIS publications feed and check iaisweb.org monthly for revised ICPs, ComFrame material, application papers and consultation outcomes.
For each publication record the document title, adoption date, effective date and the ICP numbers it touches in the obligations register.
Download and date-stamp the consolidated ICP text relied on, since the ICPs are revised in place and a later download will not show what was read.
Open a determination task per affected ICP standard with a 30-business-day due date and assign it to a Compliance Analyst.
checklist.done: each IAIS publication has dated source text on file and a determination task per affected standard with a 30-day due date.

checklist.step: Break the ICP into individually determinable standards
actions: Split the ICP into its numbered Standards and record each on its own register row, keeping the Guidance as supporting text rather than as an obligation.
Write each standard as a single testable requirement in the firm's own words alongside the quoted source sentence.
Where a standard bundles several duties - assess, document, report, review - split it so each duty can carry its own owner and control.
Reject rows that read as themes rather than duties; 'governance is effective' cannot be owned or tested.
checklist.done: each ICP is decomposed into numbered standards, each a single testable duty with the source sentence quoted.

checklist.step: Test applicability against every licensed entity and line of business
actions: List the group's licensed entities with their jurisdictions, licence classes and lines of business written (ALL and Life & Annuity for this regulation record).
For each standard and entity answer three questions: does the entity perform the activity, does its supervisor apply this standard, and does the group-wide supervisor apply it at group level.
Record Applicable / Not applicable / Applicable at group only, with the reason in one sentence naming the activity or licence class.
Flag standards applicable at group level but not at any entity - these are the ones that fall between owners if left unassigned.
checklist.done: each standard carries an applicability call per entity with a one-sentence reason naming the activity or licence class.

checklist.step: Map each applicable standard to the local instrument that actually binds
actions: For each applicable standard identify the local rule that transposes it for that entity - the PRA Rulebook or SS reference, the Solvency II article, the BMA Insurance Code of Conduct paragraph, or the state insurance code section.
Record the local citation next to the ICP citation, since supervisors enforce the local instrument and the ICP alone is not directly enforceable against the insurer.
Where no local instrument transposes the standard, record that fact explicitly and rate the standard as a supervisory expectation rather than a legal obligation.
Note any local rule that is stricter than the ICP standard, since the stricter text sets the control design.
Sign the mapping with name and date on each row.
checklist.done: each applicable standard carries a named local instrument citation or an explicit statement that none exists, signed and dated by counsel.

checklist.step: Rate materiality and set the control expectation
actions: Rate each applicable standard High / Medium / Low on the exposure if it were not met: policyholder harm, licence risk, capital consequence, and public censure.
For High-rated standards require a named preventive control with evidence, not a policy statement, and set the minimum evidence type (register, log, filing, attestation, test result).
Set the monitoring cadence from the rating - High quarterly, Medium semi-annual, Low annual - and write it on the row.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm the High population, since it drives the compliance monitoring plan and its resourcing.
checklist.done: each applicable standard carries a materiality rating, a required evidence type and a monitoring cadence confirmed for the High population.

checklist.step: Write the determination memo per ICP with reasoning that survives challenge
actions: Write one memo per ICP setting out: the standards decomposed, the applicability call per entity with reasons, the local transposition, the materiality rating, the proposed owner and the evidence expected.
Quote the ICP text relied on with its version date and attach the dated capture as an appendix.
State explicitly what the firm is NOT doing on the strength of a 'not applicable' call, so the consequence of a wrong call is visible.
Route to Regulatory Counsel for concurrence on every 'not applicable' row before the memo is issued.
File the issued memo in the compliance evidence repository under the ICP number and the determination date.
checklist.done: each ICP has an issued, dated memo with quoted source text, per-entity reasoning and counsel concurrence on every not-applicable call.

checklist.step: Identify the right owner from the process and org map, not by convenience
actions: For each applicable standard find the process that performs the activity and the role that owns that process on the operating-model map.
Propose the owner as a named role with a named incumbent, and record the division and department they sit in.
Refuse owner proposals that name a committee, a function or 'Compliance' for a first-line duty - the owner must be able to execute the control.
Where the activity spans functions, split the standard into the parts each role can own rather than naming a joint owner.
checklist.done: each applicable standard names a single accountable role and incumbent who performs the underlying activity.

checklist.step: Obtain written acceptance from each proposed owner
actions: Send each proposed owner their standards with the requirement text, the materiality rating, the evidence expected and the monitoring cadence.
Require an explicit accept or challenge inside 10 business days; silence is recorded as not accepted, not as accepted by default.
Where an owner challenges, hold a resolution meeting with the function head and record the outcome and the reasoning on the row.
Record acceptance with the accepter's name, role and date on the register row and lock the owner field against silent reassignment.
checklist.done: every applicable standard shows a dated written acceptance by a named owner, with challenges resolved and recorded.

checklist.step: Link each accepted standard to an existing control or raise a gap
actions: Search the control library for a control that already delivers the standard and link it, recording the control identifier and its last test result.
Where the control exists but is not evidenced at the required frequency, record a control-design gap rather than linking it and moving on.
Where no control exists, raise a gap with the owner, a target design date and the interim risk position.
Produce the coverage view: standards with a tested control, with an untested control, and with no control at all.
checklist.done: every accepted standard links to a control with its last test result, or carries a dated gap with an interim risk position.

checklist.step: Deconflict against existing regulation records so obligations are not duplicated
actions: Search the obligations register for existing records covering the same duty under a local instrument (for example an AML programme obligation already recorded under the local AML law).
Where a duplicate exists, link the ICP standard to the existing obligation and its control rather than creating a second owner and a second evidence trail.
Where the ICP standard is broader than the existing record, extend the existing record's scope and note the extension.
Record the deconfliction decision on both rows so a later reader can see why there is one control and two citations.
checklist.done: each ICP standard either links to an existing obligation or stands alone, with the deconfliction decision recorded on both records.

checklist.step: Publish the determination set and the resulting monitoring plan
actions: Publish the register view by ICP, standard, applicability, owner, control and cadence to the compliance intranet page and to each function head.
Build the compliance monitoring plan for the year from the High and Medium populations and their cadences.
Present the coverage view - standards with no control and standards with no accepted owner - to the Risk and Compliance Committee as a decision item.
Record the committee's acceptance of any standard left uncontrolled with the reason and the date it will be revisited.
checklist.done: the determination set is published, the monitoring plan is built from it, and uncontrolled standards are accepted at committee with a revisit date.

checklist.step: Re-determine on trigger events
actions: Re-run the applicability test whenever a new licence or entity is added, a line of business is entered or exited, or a material outsourcing moves an activity out of the group.
Re-run it on every IAIS revision and on every local transposition change flagged by Regulatory Counsel.
Re-issue only the affected memos rather than the whole set, and version them so the prior determination stays retrievable.
Update owners where an organisational change removed the incumbent, within 10 business days of the change taking effect.
checklist.done: trigger events produce a versioned re-determination of the affected standards within their deadlines, with owners refreshed.

checklist.step: Run the annual full re-determination ahead of the self-assessment cycle
actions: Reconcile the register against the current published ICP set and list standards in the ICP set with no register row and register rows with no matching standard.
Refresh the applicability call for every standard, not only the changed ones, since entity and business-mix changes shift applicability without any ICP change.
Refresh owner names against the HR feed so no standard is owned by a leaver.
Close the cycle with a coverage statement: standards in the set, applicable, owned, controlled and evidenced, with the four numbers reconciling.
checklist.done: the annual cycle closes with a reconciled coverage statement whose counts tie to the current published ICP set.

checklist.step: Build the ICP self-assessment matrix supervisors will ask for
actions: Export one row per ICP standard with applicability, local instrument, owner role and incumbent, control identifier, evidence location and last evidence date.
Add a short observed-practice statement per High-rated standard describing how the firm meets it, drawn from the control description rather than written fresh.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the matrix for statements that overclaim compliance against standards with untested controls.
File the matrix version with its export date so a supervisory request can be answered from the version in force at the time.
checklist.done: a dated self-assessment matrix exists with one row per standard, counsel-reviewed and free of claims unsupported by tested controls.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence for the retention period
actions: File the memos, dated ICP text captures, counsel concurrences, owner acceptances and register version exports under the determination date.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label so a superseded determination survives to explain a historic position.
Index by ICP number, standard number, entity and determination date.
Confirm the superseded versions remain retrievable rather than overwritten in place.
checklist.done: determination evidence is filed with 7-year retention, indexed by ICP and entity, with superseded versions still retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of ICP standards and register determinations
actions: Extract every register row for this regulation with ICP number, standard number, entity, applicability, local instrument, owner, control and determination date.
Take the current published consolidated ICP set as the independent completeness source and count its standards.
Record extract date, counts and query in the workpaper before sampling.
List every entity dimension missing from the register, since a determination made for the group but not for a licensed entity is an incomplete population.
testing.done: the register population is extracted by ICP, standard and entity with missing entity dimensions isolated.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the published ICP set
actions: Match register rows to the published standards on ICP number and standard number and list standards with no row.
List register rows citing a standard number that no longer exists in the current text, which signals determinations made against a superseded version.
Compare the dated ICP text capture on file with the current published version and note any standard revised since the determination date.
Treat any unmatched published standard as a coverage failure of the framework, not a single-row exception.
testing.done: the register reconciles to the published ICP set, with missing standards and stale-version determinations listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of standards rated High, 100% of rows determined 'not applicable', and 100% of standards determined in the period under test.
Take 20 further rows at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, spread across entities.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every standard with an open framework gap from the prior period as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all High-rated, not-applicable and newly determined standards.

testing.step: Re-perform the applicability call independently
actions: Read the ICP standard text and the entity's licence class and activities, and reach your own applicability conclusion before reading the recorded call.
Test the recorded reason against the entity's actual business - a 'not applicable, we do not write that business' call fails if the entity writes it.
Compare to the recorded determination; a right answer supported by a wrong or absent reason is still an exception.
Capture the standard text and the licence evidence relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent applicability conclusion with the source text and licence evidence captured.

testing.step: Verify the local transposition citation actually says what is claimed
actions: Open the cited local instrument for each sampled applicable row and read the provision as it stood on the determination date.
Confirm the provision covers the duty in the ICP standard and note where the local rule is stricter, since the control must be built to the stricter text.
Flag rows citing a repealed or renumbered provision.
Confirm rows recorded as having no local transposition genuinely have none rather than the mapping simply not having been done.
testing.done: each sampled transposition citation is verified as in force and as covering the duty, with stricter local text flagged.

testing.step: Test owner assignment and acceptance
actions: For each sampled applicable row confirm a named role and incumbent is recorded and that the incumbent is a current employee in the HR system.
Confirm a dated written acceptance exists and that its date falls within 10 business days of the determination issue date.
Test that the owner performs the underlying activity by comparing the role to the process owner on the operating-model map - a first-line duty owned by Compliance is an exception.
List standards whose owner has left, changed role or never accepted.
testing.done: every sampled applicable standard has a current, activity-performing owner with a timely written acceptance.

testing.step: Test control linkage and evidence currency
actions: For each sampled row open the linked control and confirm it exists, is in scope for the same entity and has a test result within its stated cadence.
Compare the evidence type held to the evidence type the determination required, and flag policy documents standing in for operational evidence.
List standards linked to a control whose last test failed and was not remediated.
Treat a standard with no control and no dated gap record as an unmanaged obligation.
testing.done: every sampled standard's control linkage is verified for scope, cadence and evidence type, with unmanaged obligations listed.

testing.step: Recompute the determination turnaround against the deadlines
actions: For each publication in the period compute business days from the publication or adoption date to the determination memo issue date and compare to the 30-business-day standard.
Compute business days from memo issue to owner acceptance and compare to the 10-business-day standard.
List every breach with the days over, and check whether any extension was approved by the Head of Compliance in writing.
Test that the trigger-event re-determinations for new entities or licences happened within their own deadlines.
testing.done: turnaround times are recomputed against the 30-day and 10-day standards with every breach quantified in days.

testing.step: Test the self-assessment matrix against the register behind it
actions: Take the most recently exported self-assessment matrix and reconcile its row count and owner names to the register as at the export date.
Read the observed-practice statements for five High-rated standards and confirm each is supported by the linked control's evidence rather than by intent.
Flag any statement claiming compliance where the linked control has no test result.
Confirm the matrix version in force at each historic supervisory request is still retrievable.
testing.done: the matrix reconciles to the register and every sampled observed-practice statement is supported by tested control evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions, obtain independent sign-off and conclude
actions: Raise one issue per exception with ICP and standard number, entity, the element failed and the obligation left unmanaged, assigning a root cause from a fixed list (standard not determined, applicability unsupported, transposition wrong, owner not accepted, control absent, turnaround breached) with an owner and remediation date.
Compute determination coverage, owner acceptance rate and control linkage rate against the zero-gap threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the reconciliation and re-performance workpapers.

Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled determination and does not report to the Head of Compliance, sign the workpaper; report to the Risk and Compliance Committee and file the workpaper indexed by review period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, acceptance and linkage rates, with every exception owned, dated and reported to committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Coordinates delivery across the first-line owners assigned under REG-013-C53 and holds the implementation plan; each individual action stays owned by its assigned first-line role, and slippage on a High-rated standard escalates to the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - implementation is driven from the determination memos, so each action carries forward the ICP and Standard number determined for it (this item's carried citations are ICP 22 Standard 22.3 and ICP 15 Standards 15.6-15.8) together with the local instrument that binds the entity; the citation on the action is re-checked against the memo at design sign-off so a control is never built to a superseded requirement text

In-scope processes.value: Implementation of every applicable ICP standard accepted by an owner: control design, procedure change, system or report change, training, first execution, evidence capture and hand-over into business-as-usual monitoring

In-scope systems.value: Action plan, control records, evidence links and attestations; delivery tracked in the PPM tool where a change project is required; evidence itself filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Obligation Implementation Procedure - action planning from the determination memo, control design standard (who, what, when, what evidence), design sign-off, first-execution proof, evidence naming and filing convention, and the rules for closing an action

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Risk Officer's endorsement of the closure rules, since closure is what converts a plan into an asserted control

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Implementation plan agreed within 20 business days of owner acceptance; High-rated standards implemented within 90 days, Medium within 180 days, Low by the next annual cycle; first execution evidenced within one cadence period of go-live; monthly delivery report to the Risk and Compliance Committee

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC action records carry due dates with reminders to the owner at T-30, T-14 and T-3 days and automatic escalation to the function head on the due date, plus a weekly overdue-action report to the Compliance Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Action plan, design sign-off, first-execution evidence, each cadence period's operating evidence and the closure attestation retained 7 years from the action's closure date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: An action closed without first-execution evidence, an overdue action on a High-rated standard, or a control operating without producing its stated evidence is logged as an implementation failure with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs off any High-rated standard whose implementation is extended beyond 90 days and any action closed on compensating controls rather than the designed control

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All implementation actions raised from the determination memos and open or closed during the period, joined to their control records and to the evidence actually filed for each cadence period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: An action may only be closed with a design sign-off, dated first-execution evidence and a named evidence location; closure without any one of the three fails. Zero High-rated standards may sit overdue without a written CRO extension. Evidence completeness threshold: at least 95% of required cadence periods hold the stated evidence, with no gaps on High-rated standards.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per item and continuous, so the test runs quarterly over actions closed that quarter plus a rolling evidence-completeness check on controls already in business-as-usual, and annually across the full action population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed, designed or signed off any sampled action and must sit outside the implementing function

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly implementation assurance workpaper (action extract, closure testing, evidence completeness matrix, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by ICP standard and quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per standard: the determination memo, the control description, the design sign-off and the last four cadence periods of operating evidence, assembled for a supervisory college or thematic review within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager coordinates the supervisory request; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement that a control is operating effectively where the evidence is incomplete, and the Head of Compliance approves what is filed

checklist.step: Turn each accepted standard into a dated action plan with the owner
actions: Open the determination memo and, with the accepted owner, list the concrete deliverables: procedure change, control build, system or report change, training and evidence capture.
Set the due date from the materiality rating - 90 days High, 180 days Medium, next annual cycle Low - measured from owner acceptance.
Record for each deliverable the owner, the contributing functions and the dependency on any system release.
Raise each deliverable as a GRC action with its own due date rather than one action per standard, so partial delivery is visible.
Have the owner confirm the plan is deliverable with their current resourcing, or escalate the resourcing gap to the function head in writing the same week.
checklist.done: each accepted standard has deliverable-level actions with owners, due dates set from the materiality rating, and a confirmed resourcing position.

checklist.step: Design the control so it names who does what, when, and what falls out
actions: Write the control description in the standard form: the role that performs it, the trigger or frequency, the specific step performed, the threshold or criterion applied, and the artifact produced.
Set the control type (preventive or detective) and whether it is manual, IT-dependent manual or automated, and name the system report it depends on.
Name the evidence artifact precisely - not 'documentation' but 'the dated screening exception report signed by the reviewer'.
Define the failure condition so a monitoring reviewer can tell a pass from a fail without asking the performer.
Reject designs whose evidence is the absence of a problem; a control that produces nothing cannot be tested.
checklist.done: each control has a description naming performer, frequency, step, criterion, artifact and failure condition.

checklist.step: Get design sign-off before the control is built
actions: Test the design on paper against the requirement text in the determination memo, clause by clause, and record where each clause is met.
Check the frequency in the design is at least as often as the requirement demands and that the population the control covers is the full in-scope population.
Have the owner and the Compliance Officer both sign the design record with names and dates.
Return designs that meet the requirement only for part of the population - partial coverage discovered later is the most common implementation failure.
checklist.done: each control design carries a clause-by-clause mapping to the requirement and dual dated sign-off before build starts.

checklist.step: Change the written procedure the staff actually follow
actions: Amend the operating procedure at the exact step where the control sits, showing the input, the check, the decision rule and where the artifact is filed.
Version the procedure, record the effective date and retire the prior version so only one procedure is live.
Have the process owner approve the change and the Compliance Officer confirm it matches the signed design.
Publish the change to the team with a named effective date rather than letting it take effect silently on save.
checklist.done: the live procedure carries the control step at the right point, versioned, dated and approved against the signed design.

checklist.step: Build the system or report change the control depends on
actions: Write the requirement as a story naming the data fields, the report layout, the filter logic and the retention of the output.
Confirm with the Data Governance Lead that every field the control relies on is populated and governed, since a control built on an optional field will fail silently.
Have the QA Analyst test the report against a known population and confirm record counts and totals reconcile to the source system.
Schedule the report to run automatically at the control frequency and to deliver to the performer, so operation does not depend on someone remembering.
checklist.done: the supporting report or system change is built, reconciled to source on counts and totals, and scheduled at the control frequency.

checklist.step: Train the people who will perform and review the control
actions: Build a short role-based module covering the requirement, the control step, the decision rule and what to do when the control fails.
Assign it to the performing team and the reviewing role with a completion deadline before the control's go-live date.
Include a worked example using a real (anonymised) case rather than an abstract description.
Report completion to the owner and block go-live where the performing team is below full completion.
checklist.done: the performing and reviewing populations have completed role-based training before go-live, with completion evidenced.

checklist.step: Run the first execution and prove it produced the artifact
actions: Observe or re-perform the first execution of the control alongside the performer and record the date, the population it covered and the outcome.
Confirm the artifact named in the design was actually produced, is dated, identifies the performer and shows the criterion applied.
Where the first execution surfaced a design flaw - wrong population, unavailable data, unclear criterion - reopen the design rather than patching it verbally.
Attach the first-execution artifact to the action record as the evidence that converts a plan into an operating control.
checklist.done: the first execution is observed, dated and evidenced by the designed artifact, or the design is reopened.

checklist.step: Fix the evidence naming, filing location and retention
actions: Create the evidence folder in the compliance evidence repository named <ICP>-<standard>-<entity> and record its path on the control record.
Set the naming convention for each period's artifact as <control id>-<period end date>-<performer initials> so a missing period is visible by inspection.
Apply the retention label required by the obligation - 7 years from closure as the standing rule, longer where the local instrument demands it.
Grant the monitoring reviewer read access so evidence gathering never depends on chasing the performer.
checklist.done: each control has a named evidence location, a period-based naming convention, a retention label and reviewer read access.

checklist.step: Close the action only against the closure rules
actions: Check the three closure conditions: signed design, dated first-execution evidence, and a populated evidence location on the control record.
Reject closure requests supported by a procedure document alone, since a written procedure is design, not operation.

Where the designed control could not be built and a compensating control is proposed, document the compensating control, the residual gap and obtain the Chief Risk Officer's written acceptance before closing.
Stamp the closure with the closer's name and date and move the control into the monitoring plan at its stated cadence.
checklist.done: no action is closed without design sign-off, first-execution evidence and an evidence location, and compensating closures carry CRO acceptance.

checklist.step: Hand the control into business-as-usual monitoring
actions: Add the control to the compliance monitoring plan at the cadence set in the determination, naming the monitoring tester and the sample approach.
Set the first monitoring review for one cadence period after go-live so a failing control is caught inside its first cycle.
Brief the monitoring tester on the failure condition from the design so the review tests operation, not existence.
Record the hand-over date on the control record.
checklist.done: each closed action's control appears in the monitoring plan with a named tester and a first review inside one cadence period.

checklist.step: Track delivery and escalate slippage before the due date
actions: Maintain the implementation plan with percent complete, dependencies and the critical path for actions requiring a system release.
Flag any action forecast to breach its due date at least 30 days ahead and take the owner's written recovery plan or extension request.
Route High-rated extensions to the Chief Risk Officer for written approval; Medium and Low to the Head of Compliance.
Report weekly to the Compliance Manager on overdue actions by materiality rating with days overdue.
checklist.done: forecast breaches are flagged 30 days ahead with a recovery plan or an approved extension, and overdue ageing is reported weekly.

checklist.step: Capture the operating evidence every cadence period
actions: Run a monthly sweep of the evidence folders and list controls with no artifact filed for the last completed period.
Chase the performer within 5 business days and record whether the control was performed and not filed, or not performed at all - the two are different findings.
Escalate any High-rated control missing two consecutive periods to the owner's function head.
Publish the evidence completeness matrix - control by period - to the Compliance Manager monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly completeness matrix shows evidence filed per control per period, distinguishing not-filed from not-performed.

checklist.step: Feed control failures back into design rather than logging them and moving on
actions: Where a control fails at monitoring, establish whether the failure is design (the control cannot meet the requirement) or operation (it was not performed properly).
Send design failures back through the design sign-off step with the owner and the Compliance Officer, and re-run first execution.
For operation failures, agree the specific fix - report scheduling, staffing, training refresh - with a date, rather than a general instruction to be more careful.
Record the failure, the classification and the fix on the control record so repeat failures are visible over time.
checklist.done: each control failure is classified design or operation, with design failures re-signed and re-executed and operation failures given a dated fix.

checklist.step: Report implementation status to the Risk and Compliance Committee
actions: Report actions raised, closed, overdue and extended, split by materiality rating, with the ICP standards behind the overdue population named.
Report the evidence completeness rate for controls already in business-as-usual and name any High-rated control with gaps.
Table each requested extension on a High-rated standard with the residual exposure and the CRO's recommendation.
Have the minute record the accepted extensions and the date each will be revisited.
checklist.done: the committee minute records delivery status by materiality, evidence completeness and each accepted extension with a revisit date.

checklist.step: Retain the implementation evidence set
actions: File the action plan, design sign-off, procedure version, training completion, first-execution artifact and closure attestation under the ICP standard and entity.
Apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label and confirm the label survives any folder restructure.
Index by ICP number, standard, entity, control identifier and closure date so a supervisory request can be answered by search.
Confirm each closed action's evidence location still resolves, since moved folders silently break the control record's link.
checklist.done: the implementation evidence set is filed, retention-labelled, indexed by standard and control, with every evidence link verified to resolve.

testing.step: Build the population of implementation actions and their controls
actions: Extract every action raised from the determination memos with ICP standard, entity, owner, materiality rating, due date, status and closure date.
Extract the linked control records with description, frequency, evidence location and last monitoring result.
Join the two and list actions with no linked control and controls with no originating action.
Record extract date, counts and query in the workpaper before sampling.
testing.done: the action and control populations are joined, with orphan actions and orphan controls already isolated.

testing.step: Reconcile the action population back to the determination register
actions: Extract every applicable, accepted standard from the obligations register and match it to at least one implementation action.
List applicable standards with no action raised - these are obligations accepted and then never implemented, the failure this test exists to find.
Check that standards whose determination was revised have had their actions revised too, rather than delivering to a superseded requirement.
Treat any High-rated standard with no action as a framework failure, not a single-row exception.
testing.done: every accepted applicable standard traces to an action, and High-rated standards with none are escalated as framework failures.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of actions on High-rated standards, 100% of actions closed in the period, and 100% of actions closed on compensating controls.
Take 15 further actions at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population across entities and owners.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every action with a prior-period implementation failure as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all High-rated, newly closed and compensating-control actions.

testing.step: Test closures against the three closure conditions
actions: For each sampled closed action open the design sign-off and confirm it is dated before the build and signed by both the owner and the Compliance Officer.
Open the first-execution artifact and confirm it is dated, names the performer, shows the criterion applied and covers the full in-scope population.
Confirm the evidence location on the control record resolves to a folder that actually contains artifacts.
Record a closure as failed where any of the three conditions is absent, regardless of how well the control is now operating.
testing.done: each sampled closure is tested against design sign-off, dated first-execution evidence and a resolving evidence location.

testing.step: Re-perform the design-to-requirement mapping
actions: Read the requirement text from the determination memo and the control description, and independently map clause to control step.
Test frequency sufficiency: a quarterly control cannot satisfy a requirement demanding action on every transaction.
Test population sufficiency: confirm the control's population equals the requirement's in-scope population for the entity, not a convenient subset.
Record every clause the control does not reach as a design gap, with the exposure it leaves.
testing.done: each sampled control is independently mapped clause by clause, with frequency and population sufficiency tested and gaps quantified.

testing.step: Re-perform the control on a sample of periods
actions: For five sampled controls take one operating period each and re-perform the control step from the same source data the performer used.
Compare your outcome to the artifact filed, including the exceptions the performer identified and how they were dispositioned.
Flag artifacts that record a clean result where re-performance finds items the criterion should have caught.
Capture the source data extract and your working into the workpaper.
testing.done: five controls are re-performed from source data with outcomes compared to the filed artifact and differences logged.

testing.step: Test evidence completeness across cadence periods
actions: For each sampled control build the expected period list from its frequency and go-live date, and compare it to the artifacts actually filed.
Compute the completeness percentage per control and against the 95% threshold, with zero tolerance on High-rated controls.
For each missing period establish whether the control was performed and not filed or not performed, using the performer's system activity as corroboration.
List controls whose artifacts are all created on the same date, which indicates retrospective assembly rather than periodic operation.
testing.done: completeness is computed per control against the threshold, with missing periods classified and retrospective assembly flagged.

testing.step: Recompute delivery timeliness and test extensions
actions: Recompute each sampled action's due date from the owner acceptance date and the materiality rating (90/180 days or next annual cycle).
Compare to the recorded due date and to the actual closure date, and list actions closed late or with a due date silently moved.
For every extension on a High-rated standard confirm a written CRO approval exists and pre-dates the original due date.
Quantify total days of slippage on High-rated standards as the headline exposure figure.
testing.done: due dates are recomputed from acceptance dates, late closures and silent date changes are listed, and High-rated extensions are traced to prior CRO approval.

testing.step: Test compensating-control closures and residual gaps
actions: Pull every sampled action closed on a compensating control and read the documented residual gap and the CRO acceptance.
Test whether the compensating control actually addresses the requirement clause the designed control was to meet, or merely detects the same failure later.
Confirm a date is set to revisit the compensating position and that it has not passed unactioned.
Treat a compensating closure with no documented residual gap as an unsupported closure.
testing.done: each compensating closure is tested against the requirement clause, with a documented residual gap, CRO acceptance and a live revisit date.

testing.step: Log exceptions, obtain independent sign-off and conclude
actions: Raise one issue per exception with ICP standard, entity, action, the closure condition or evidence period failed and the obligation left unevidenced, assigning a root cause from a fixed list (no action raised, design gap, closed without first execution, evidence not filed, control not performed, late closure) with an owner and remediation date.
Compute the valid-closure rate, the evidence completeness rate and the High-rated on-time delivery rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the re-performance and completeness workpapers.

Have the independent reviewer, who designed, performed and signed off none of the sampled actions, sign the workpaper; report to the Risk and Compliance Committee and file the workpaper indexed by quarter and ICP standard.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states valid-closure, evidence completeness and on-time delivery rates, with every exception owned and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the sanctions screening programme across the policy lifecycle - applicant, insured, beneficial owner, beneficiary, assignee, payee and producer - and personally owns the blocking and reporting decision on a confirmed match

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 22 Standard 22.6 (targeted financial sanctions) read in the consolidated ICP text, together with the instruments that actually bind: OFAC 31 CFR Part 501 reporting and the SDN and Consolidated Sanctions lists, EU Council Regulation consolidated list, UK OFSI consolidated list under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, and the UN Security Council Consolidated List; list versions and their publication dates are recorded at each screening run

In-scope processes.value: Screening at new business application and pre-bind, at policy issue, at every beneficiary or assignee change, at payee set-up, at claim payment and surrender or annuity disbursement, at producer appointment, and daily rescreening of the entire in-force book against list updates - across ALL and Life & Annuity

In-scope systems.value: Screening engine holding the list feeds, matching rules and alert queue; parties fed from the policy administration system and payees from the payment gateway; alert dispositions written back to the party record

Compliance procedure documented.value: Sanctions Screening and Blocking Procedure - screening points and the data fields screened, list coverage and refresh frequency, matching thresholds and fuzzy logic settings, alert triage levels and turnaround times, escalation to confirmed match, blocking and rejection handling, and the OFAC reporting timetable

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel concurrence on the blocking and reporting sections; re-approved annually and on any change to matching thresholds or list coverage

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: List refresh within 24 hours of publication and rescreening of the book on each refresh; level-1 alerts triaged same business day and level-2 within 3 business days; blocked property and rejected transaction reports filed with OFAC within 10 business days of the action; Annual Report of Blocked Property filed by 30 September for the preceding year; SAR filed within 30 calendar days where the match reveals suspicious activity

Deadline reminders configured.value: Alert queue SLA timers page the duty Sanctions Analyst at 50% and the Financial Crime AML Officer at 90% of the triage window; a standing calendar task fires at T-30 to the 30 September annual blocked-property report; blocked-item records auto-raise the 10-business-day report task on the block date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Screening run logs with list version and timestamp, alert records with disposition and reviewer, match evidence, blocking instructions, OFAC filings with confirmation numbers and the annual report retained 5 years minimum under the sanctions record-keeping rules and 7 years under group policy

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A party bound or paid without a screening record, an alert closed outside its SLA, a threshold change made without approval, or a late OFAC report is logged as a sanctions control breach with root cause, owner and self-report decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every false-positive closure of a level-1 alert on a name matching an SDN entry, every unblocked release of a held payment, and every late or amended OFAC filing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All parties created or changed in the period (applicants, insureds, owners, beneficial owners, beneficiaries, assignees, payees, producers) and all outbound payments made in the period, taken from the policy administration system and the payment gateway, joined to the screening system's run and alert logs

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any party bound and any payment released with no screening record before the event is a fail, and any confirmed match paid rather than blocked is a reportable breach. Alert SLA threshold: at least 98% of alerts triaged inside their window with no level-1 breaches. Any false-positive closure without recorded discriminating data (date of birth, address, identifier) fails.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so the test runs monthly on a rolling basis over that month's parties and payments, with a full quarterly review including matching-threshold tuning evidence and an annual end-to-end test before the 30 September blocked-property report

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside financial crime operations and must not have dispositioned any sampled alert

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly and quarterly sanctions screening workpapers (party and payment extracts, screening log reconciliation, alert sample, re-screening results, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by period

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening coverage evidence - list versions and run logs, matching configuration with approval, alert dispositions with discriminating data, blocked-item file with OFAC confirmation numbers and the annual report - producible for an OFAC enquiry, an OFSI request or a supervisory ICP 22 review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Financial Crime AML Officer owns the OFAC and OFSI contact; Regulatory Counsel clears every licence application, voluntary self-disclosure and any response admitting a released payment; the Head of Compliance approves what is filed

checklist.step: Maintain the sanctions list feeds and record the version screened against
actions: Confirm the daily automated feed loaded each list: OFAC SDN and Consolidated (Non-SDN) lists, the EU consolidated list, the UK OFSI consolidated list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and any local list for jurisdictions the group writes in.
Check the load report for each list's publication date and record count, and investigate any list whose count did not change across an OFAC update announcement.
Record the list version identifier and load timestamp against every screening run, so a later question about a specific date can be answered exactly.
Raise an incident where any list is more than 24 hours stale and suspend straight-through binding for affected products until it is refreshed.
File the daily load report in the evidence folder for the month.
checklist.done: each list shows a dated load within 24 hours of publication, with version identifiers recorded against every screening run.

checklist.step: Screen the applicant and all connected parties before binding
actions: At application, submit for screening every party on the case: proposed insured, policy owner, payer, beneficial owners of a corporate owner, named beneficiaries and any irrevocable assignee.

Send the full data set the engine needs to discriminate - full legal name, date of birth or incorporation, address, country of residence, nationality and any government identifier - not the name alone.
Hold the case in a screening-pending status that physically blocks issue until a clear or dispositioned result returns.
Where a party is missing a date of birth or address, obtain it before screening rather than screening on name only, since name-only screening produces alerts that cannot be discriminated.
Record the screening reference on the case so the pre-bind check can be traced from the policy record.
checklist.done: no case can be issued without a returned screening result for every connected party, screened on full identifying data.

checklist.step: Screen producers, brokers and third-party payees at onboarding
actions: At appointment, screen the producer entity, its principals and its beneficial owners alongside the licence verification run in NIPR.
Screen premium finance companies, trustees, corporate beneficiaries and any third-party payee before they are set up in the payment master.
Re-screen the producer population monthly and on every appointment renewal, since ownership changes do not announce themselves.
Block appointment and commission payment where a party is pending disposition, and record the block on the producer record.
checklist.done: every producer, principal and third-party payee is screened before appointment or payee set-up and re-screened monthly.

checklist.step: Rescreen the in-force book on every list update
actions: Run the full book rescreen against each refreshed list, covering every party role held on in-force and recently lapsed policies, not just current policy owners.
Reconcile the party count submitted to the party count in the policy administration system for the same date and investigate any shortfall before accepting the run.
Record the run identifier, list version, party count and alert count in the run log.
Escalate a run that completes with zero alerts across a large list update to the Model Risk Analyst as a possible configuration failure rather than a good day.
checklist.done: each list refresh produces a full-book rescreen whose party count reconciles to the policy administration system, with the run logged.

checklist.step: Triage alerts to the SLA with recorded discriminating data
actions: Work the alert queue by level: level-1 (strong name and secondary identifier match) same business day, level-2 within 3 business days.

For each alert compare at least two discriminating attributes - date of birth, place of birth, address, nationality, passport or national identifier - between the customer record and the list entry, and record both values in the disposition.
Close as false positive only where a discriminator differs conclusively; record which attribute cleared it, never 'reviewed - not a match'.
Escalate to potential true match where discriminators are absent or agree, and freeze any pending transaction for that party immediately.
Have a second analyst review every level-1 false-positive closure before it is committed.
checklist.done: every alert is closed inside its SLA with the discriminating attributes and their values recorded, and level-1 closures peer-reviewed.

checklist.step: Investigate and confirm potential true matches
actions: Pull the full list entry from the issuing authority's own record, including all aliases, addresses, identifiers and the programme under which the party is designated.
Gather the customer file: application, identification documents, payment history, beneficiary changes and any adverse media, and compare identity attributes point by point.

Where identity remains ambiguous, request additional identification from the customer through a channel that does not tip off the party about the sanctions review, and take Regulatory Counsel's guidance on wording.
Write the investigation conclusion - confirmed match, not a match, or unresolved - with the evidence relied on and a recommendation.
Escalate every confirmed match to the Financial Crime AML Officer the same day.
checklist.done: each potential true match has a documented attribute-by-attribute investigation and a same-day escalation where confirmed.

checklist.step: Block or reject and stop the money the same day
actions: On a confirmed match, instruct the Treasury Manager to place the funds in a blocked interest-bearing account where the property must be blocked, or to reject and return the transaction where the programme requires rejection - the two are different obligations and produce different reports.
Suspend the policy transaction: stop the payment, freeze surrender and loan processing, and prevent further premium application without instruction.
Record the date and time of the block or rejection, the amount, the currency, the counterparty and the programme, since the OFAC report is built from these fields.
Instruct the Contact Center Ops Manager on the approved holding language for any customer contact, cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer and the General Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: the funds are blocked or rejected the same day with amount, currency, counterparty and programme recorded, and the policy transaction suspended.

checklist.step: File the blocked property or rejected transaction report within 10 business days
actions: Prepare the report with the blocking or rejection date, the property description, the amount and currency, the ownership interest, the sanctions programme and the account where blocked funds are held.
Submit through OFAC's reporting channel within 10 business days of the block or rejection and capture the confirmation reference.
File the equivalent report to OFSI or the relevant EU competent authority where the designation arises under those regimes, on their own forms and deadlines.
Attach the filed report and confirmation to the case record and to the blocked-item register.
Where a licence will be sought to release or deal with the property, instruct Regulatory Counsel to prepare the application and record the licence number on the item.
checklist.done: each blocked or rejected item has a report filed within 10 business days with a confirmation reference on the case record.

checklist.step: Assess whether the match also requires a suspicious activity report
actions: Review the customer file for indicators beyond the designation itself - structuring, third-party premium payment, rapid surrender, or use of the policy as a value transfer.
Where suspicion arises, prepare the SAR narrative covering who, what, when, where and why, referencing the sanctions match without disclosing the filing to the customer.
File within 30 calendar days of initial detection through the BSA E-Filing System and record the BSA identifier.
Store the SAR and its supporting documentation in the restricted-access folder, separate from the general case file, and record only the fact of filing on the case.
checklist.done: the SAR assessment is documented for every confirmed match and, where filed, the BSA identifier is recorded with restricted-access storage.

checklist.step: Maintain the blocked-item register and file the annual report by 30 September
actions: Keep a register of every blocked item with block date, amount, currency, accrued interest, programme, report reference and current status.
Reconcile the register to the blocked account balances with the Treasury Analyst monthly, including interest credited.
Prepare the Annual Report of Blocked Property covering property held as at 30 June and file it by 30 September, and keep the filed copy with its confirmation.
Confirm no item has been released without a licence, and list the licence number against any released item.
checklist.done: the blocked-item register reconciles monthly to account balances and the annual report is filed by 30 September with confirmation retained.

checklist.step: Govern the matching thresholds and tune them on evidence
actions: Record the current matching configuration: fuzzy match scores by field, name-culture handling, thresholds by party type and any suppression rules.

Require a documented change request with before-and-after testing for every threshold or suppression change, approved by the Financial Crime AML Officer and the Head of Compliance - loosening a threshold silently is the classic screening failure.
Run an annual above-and-below-the-line test: sample cleared items just below the alert threshold and confirm none is a genuine match.
Run a known-match test by injecting seeded test names drawn from current list entries and confirm each is detected in the same run.
File the configuration version, the tuning results and the approvals in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the matching configuration is versioned and approved, with annual below-the-line and seeded known-match testing evidenced.

checklist.step: Screen at the payment point as well as the party point
actions: Screen every outbound payment instruction - claim settlement, surrender, annuity payment, commission, refund and vendor payment - against the lists at release, including the payee bank and any intermediary named on the instruction.
Hold any payment with an open alert in a pending queue that cannot be released by the requesting business unit.
Reconcile daily the count of payments released to the count of payments screened, and investigate any difference before the next release cycle.
Record the screening reference on the payment record so a payment can be tied to its screening run.
checklist.done: every outbound payment is screened at release with a recorded screening reference and a daily released-versus-screened reconciliation.

checklist.step: Train the front-line and test their handling of a hit
actions: Assign annual sanctions training to new business, underwriting, claims, payments, distribution and contact centre staff, covering what a hit looks like, the prohibition on tipping off and the escalation route.
Include a scenario exercise where the learner must decide whether to release a payment with an open alert.
Track completion with a 30-day deadline and escalate non-completion to the function head.
Record completion rates by function for the compliance monitoring report.
checklist.done: annual sanctions training is completed by every screening-adjacent function with completion tracked and escalated.

checklist.step: Monitor screening coverage daily so gaps surface within a day
actions: Build a daily coverage dashboard comparing parties created in the policy administration system to parties screened, and payments released to payments screened.
Investigate every unscreened party or payment the same day, and record whether the cause was an interface failure, a manual bypass or a data-quality reject.
Track the alert queue ageing against SLA and the false-positive rate by rule, since a spiking false-positive rate precedes analysts closing alerts carelessly.
Report daily exceptions to the Financial Crime AML Officer and weekly trends to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a daily dashboard reconciles parties and payments to screening runs, with every gap investigated and classified the same day.

checklist.step: Retain the screening evidence for the record-keeping period
actions: File the daily list load reports, run logs, alert dispositions, investigation files, blocking instructions, OFAC filings and the annual report by period.
Apply a retention label of at least 5 years from the transaction or the disposition date, and 7 years under group policy, whichever is longer.
Keep SAR material in the restricted folder with access limited to the financial crime team and counsel.
Index by party, policy number, alert identifier and payment reference so an OFAC enquiry naming a person can be answered by search.
checklist.done: screening evidence is filed and retention-labelled, SAR material is access-restricted, and records are searchable by party and payment reference.

testing.step: Build the population of parties and payments requiring screening
actions: Extract every party created or changed in the period by role - applicant, insured, owner, beneficial owner, beneficiary, assignee, payee, producer - with the creation or change timestamp.
Extract every outbound payment released in the period from the payment gateway with amount, payee and release timestamp.
Record extract dates, counts and queries in the workpaper before sampling.
Confirm the extract includes beneficiary and assignee changes on in-force policies, the population most often missed by screening interfaces.
testing.done: the party and payment populations are extracted with timestamps, including in-force beneficiary and assignee changes.

testing.step: Reconcile the populations to the screening system's run logs
actions: Match every party to a screening record with a timestamp earlier than the bind or change effective time, and every payment to a screening record earlier than release.
List unmatched parties and payments, and separately list those screened after the event, since screening after payment does not satisfy the obligation.
Reconcile the full-book rescreen party counts to the in-force party counts for the same dates and investigate shortfalls.
Treat any bind or payment with no prior screening record as an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
testing.done: every party and payment is matched to a prior screening record, with unscreened and late-screened items listed as automatic exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of level-1 alerts, 100% of confirmed matches and blocked or rejected items, and 100% of alerts closed by a single analyst without peer review.
Take 40 alerts at random with a recorded seed from the level-2 false-positive population, plus 25 parties and 25 payments at random from the screened population.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-period sanctions exception as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all level-1 alerts, confirmed matches and unreviewed closures.

testing.step: Re-perform the alert disposition on the sampled alerts
actions: For each sampled alert open the list entry as it stood on the alert date and the customer record, and reach your own match conclusion before reading the disposition.

Confirm the recorded disposition names the discriminating attribute and the two values compared; a closure resting on 'reviewed' or 'common name' is a fail regardless of whether the conclusion was right.
Check the customer record actually held a date of birth or identifier at the time - a false-positive call made without discriminating data is unsupported.
Capture the list entry and the customer record into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled alert has an independent conclusion with the list entry and customer record captured, and unsupported closures listed.

testing.step: Recompute alert SLA and screening timing
actions: For each sampled alert compute business hours from alert generation to disposition and compare to the level-1 same-day and level-2 three-business-day windows.
Compute the SLA compliance rate against the 98% threshold and list every level-1 breach individually.
For sampled parties and payments compute the interval between screening and the bind or release, and flag any screened after the fact.
Recompute the list load latency from publication date to load timestamp for each list day in the period and list any day exceeding 24 hours.
testing.done: SLA compliance, screening-to-event intervals and list load latency are independently recomputed with every breach listed.

testing.step: Test the blocking and OFAC reporting on confirmed matches
actions: For each confirmed match trace the funds to a blocked interest-bearing account or to a documented rejection and return, and confirm the treatment matches the programme's requirement.
Recompute 10 business days from the block or rejection date and compare to the filing date on the confirmation reference.
Confirm the filed report's amount, currency, counterparty and programme agree with the blocked-item register and the accounting entry.
Confirm no blocked item was released without a licence number recorded, and read any licence to confirm it covers the release made.
testing.done: every confirmed match traces to the correct blocking or rejection treatment, a timely filing and, where released, a covering licence.

testing.step: Test the matching configuration and tuning evidence
actions: Compare the live matching configuration to the approved version and list any threshold, suppression rule or field weighting changed without an approved change request.
Re-run a seeded known-match test by submitting names drawn from the current OFAC SDN list through the production screening path and confirm each generates an alert.
Perform a below-the-line test on 50 records that scored just under the alert threshold and confirm none is a genuine match.
List any suppression rule that excludes a whole party role, product or country from screening as a coverage failure rather than a tuning choice.
testing.done: the live configuration matches the approved version, seeded names all alert, below-the-line testing finds no misses and blanket suppressions are listed.

testing.step: Test screening coverage by party role and product
actions: For 25 sampled policies list every party on the policy from the policy record and confirm each role appears in the screening submission, particularly beneficial owners of corporate owners and contingent beneficiaries.
Test at least one policy per product line and one per distribution channel so a channel bypassing screening is detectable.
Confirm producer and third-party payee populations were screened at onboarding and re-screened monthly.
Record any party role systematically absent from the screening feed as an interface defect affecting the whole population.
testing.done: coverage is tested role by role across products and channels, with any systematically unscreened role raised as an interface defect.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and self-report decision
actions: Raise one issue per exception with party or payment reference, what was missed and the sanctions exposure created.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (interface gap, missing identifying data, threshold loosened, alert closed without discriminators, SLA breach, late filing) and an accountable owner.
For any released payment to a confirmed match or any late filing, open a voluntary self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel and record the decision and its basis.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a self-disclosure decision where relevant and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute screening coverage (parties and payments screened before the event), the alert SLA rate and the supported-disposition rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the reconciliation, re-performance and configuration-testing workpapers.
Have the independent reviewer, who dispositioned no sampled alert and sits outside financial crime operations, sign the workpaper.
Report coverage failures and any self-disclosure to the Risk and Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper indexed by period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, SLA and disposition-support rates, with self-disclosures and coverage failures reported to committee.

In-scope processes.value: The AML programme for covered products across ALL and Life & Annuity: customer due diligence and beneficial-owner identification at application, beneficiary due diligence at claim, PEP and enhanced due diligence, risk assessment refresh, transaction monitoring, SAR decisioning, record-keeping, training, independent testing, and application of the programme to foreign branches and subsidiaries

Deadline reminders configured.value: Governance calendar tasks at T-60 and T-30 to the board approval date, at T-90 to the independent testing start, and a daily SAR ageing report flagging cases at day 20 and day 27 of the 30-day window

CDD file completeness threshold: 100% of sampled covered-product policies hold identification, beneficial-owner and risk-rating evidence dated on or before issue. Zero late SAR filings.
