Regulator-ready documentation.value: AML programme pack - current programme document, board minute designating the officer, latest risk assessment, training completion by function, independent test report with management responses, and the SAR log - producible for a FinCEN or state examination, an FCA or local supervisor request, or an ICP 22 supervisory review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Financial Crime AML Officer owns the examination contact and the document request list; Regulatory Counsel clears every response and any production touching SAR material, which is never disclosed outside the permitted channels; the Head of Compliance approves what is filed

checklist.step: Determine which products and entities the programme must cover
actions: Extract the product catalogue with each product's cash-value, investment and surrender features and its writing entity.

Classify each product as covered or not covered against the covered-product definition - permanent life with cash value, annuity contracts and any product with a cash surrender or investment feature - and record the feature that drives the call.
Confirm term life and pure group risk products excluded from the covered definition are still captured by the sanctions and general financial-crime controls, so exclusion is scoped, not blanket.
Have Regulatory Counsel concur on every product classified as not covered, and re-run the classification whenever a product is launched or repriced with new features.
Publish the covered-product list to underwriting, new business and claims so the CDD requirement follows the product.
checklist.done: every product carries a covered/not-covered classification naming the driving feature, with counsel concurrence on exclusions.

checklist.step: Refresh the enterprise AML risk assessment
actions: Score inherent risk across the four dimensions supervisors expect: customers (PEPs, non-resident, corporate and trust owners), products (single-premium annuities, high cash value, free-look and surrender features), channels (independent producers, digital direct, third-party premium payers) and geographies (jurisdictions with FATF listings or sanctions exposure).
Use actual volumes from the policy administration system for each dimension rather than qualitative impressions, and record the extract used.
Assess control effectiveness from the last independent test and monitoring results, and derive residual risk per dimension.

Document the typologies specific to insurance - early surrender with penalty accepted, overpayment and refund to a third party, beneficiary change shortly before claim, third-party premium payment - and confirm a monitoring scenario exists for each.
Take the assessment to the Board Audit Committee with the programme for approval.
checklist.done: a dated risk assessment scores inherent and residual risk on real volumes, with an insurance typology list each mapped to a monitoring scenario.

checklist.step: Update the programme document to the four pillars and the group-wide standard
actions: Update the programme to cover: internal policies, procedures and controls; the designated compliance officer with authority and resources; ongoing employee and producer training; and independent testing with a stated cycle.

Add the group-wide requirements: application of the programme to foreign branches and majority-owned subsidiaries, information sharing for AML purposes within the group, and the rule that where local law prevents application the entity applies additional measures and notifies the group.

State the CDD standard - identification and verification of the applicant, owner, payer and beneficial owners of corporate or trust owners, and beneficiary due diligence at the point of claim rather than only at issue.
State the PEP and enhanced due diligence triggers, including senior management approval to accept or continue a PEP relationship and source-of-funds evidence.
Version the document, record the effective date and retire the prior version.
checklist.done: the programme document covers all four pillars, the group-wide application rules, the CDD standard and PEP/EDD triggers in one versioned text.

checklist.step: Take the programme and the officer designation to the Board
actions: Table the programme, the risk assessment and the officer designation as a decision item at the Board Audit Committee at least annually.
Ensure the minute names the designated AML compliance officer by name and title, states the authority and resources granted, and approves the programme version by its version number.
Record the minute's date and export the extract as the evidence an examiner will ask for first.
Repeat the designation for each licensed entity that requires its own officer, rather than assuming the group designation carries.
Diarise the next annual approval on the governance calendar with T-60 and T-30 reminders.
checklist.done: a board minute within the last 12 months approves the programme by version and names the designated officer for each entity requiring one.

checklist.step: Run customer due diligence at application on every covered-product case
actions: Collect and verify identity for the proposed insured, the policy owner and the premium payer: full legal name, date of birth, residential address and a government identifier, evidenced by a document or an electronic verification result.
Where the owner is a company, partnership or trust, identify the beneficial owners at the 25% ownership threshold and the controlling person, and collect the same identifying data for each.
Record the purpose of the policy and the expected source of premium funds, and challenge premium sizes inconsistent with the stated financial profile with the Life Underwriter.
Screen for PEP status and adverse media, and route hits for enhanced due diligence before issue.
Block issue where CDD is incomplete, rather than issuing with a follow-up task - a post-issue CDD file is the finding examiners look for.
checklist.done: no covered-product policy is issued without verified identity for insured, owner and payer, beneficial owners where applicable, and a recorded source of funds.

checklist.step: Apply enhanced due diligence and senior approval to higher-risk relationships
actions: For PEPs, non-resident owners, corporate owners in higher-risk jurisdictions and large single-premium cases, gather source-of-wealth as well as source-of-funds evidence with documents, not attestations.
Record the relationship rationale and obtain the Financial Crime AML Officer's or a named senior manager's written approval before acceptance.
Set the customer risk rating in the AML system so the monitoring scenarios and the periodic review cycle follow the rating.
Diarise the periodic refresh - annually for high risk, every three years for standard - and record the next review date on the customer record.
checklist.done: every higher-risk relationship holds documented source of wealth, a written senior approval, a risk rating and a diarised refresh date.

checklist.step: Run beneficiary due diligence at the point of claim or payout
actions: At claim notification identify and verify the beneficiary, including beneficial owners where the beneficiary is a corporate entity or trust, before any payment is released.
Screen the beneficiary for PEP status and against the sanctions lists, and treat a PEP beneficiary as a trigger for enhanced scrutiny of the whole relationship before payout.
Review the beneficiary change history on the policy and escalate changes made close to the claim or to an unrelated third party to the AML Analyst.
Record the verification evidence and the screening reference on the claim file before the payment authority is granted.
checklist.done: every covered-product payout holds verified beneficiary identity, a screening reference and a reviewed beneficiary-change history before release.

checklist.step: Keep the transaction monitoring scenarios aligned to insurance typologies
actions: Maintain a scenario inventory covering early surrender with penalty accepted, overpayment followed by refund, third-party premium payment, rapid policy loan and repayment, unusual free-look cancellations and premium out of line with the customer profile.
Tune thresholds using production data and record before-and-after alert volumes and precision for every change, approved by the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Reconcile the transaction feed into the monitoring system to the policy administration and payment records daily, so a broken feed is not mistaken for a quiet day.
Review scenario coverage against the risk assessment typology list annually and add a scenario for any typology with none.
checklist.done: every typology in the risk assessment has a live scenario, tuning changes are approved with before-and-after evidence, and the feed reconciles daily.

checklist.step: Decision and file suspicious activity reports within the deadline
actions: Investigate escalated alerts by reviewing the policy history, premium sources, servicing changes and any related policies held by the same parties.
Record the decision to file or not to file with the reasoning against the suspicion standard - a not-filed decision needs the same quality of write-up as a filing.

Where filing, draft the narrative covering who, what, when, where and why, and file within 30 calendar days of initial detection (60 where no subject is identified) through the BSA E-Filing System, capturing the BSA identifier.
Consider whether continuing activity requires a continuing-activity report at 90-day intervals and diarise it.
Keep the SAR, the narrative and the supporting documents in the restricted-access folder and never disclose the filing to the customer or the producer.
checklist.done: each escalated case has a documented file/not-file decision and, where filed, a BSA identifier captured inside the 30-day window.

checklist.step: Train employees and producers on the programme every year
actions: Assign role-differentiated training: new business and underwriting on CDD and source of funds, claims on beneficiary due diligence, distribution on third-party premium and producer red flags, and the AML team on typologies and case handling.
Extend training to appointed producers selling covered products, since the programme must reach the distribution channel, and track completion through the producer management system.
Set a 30-day completion deadline, chase at 15 and 25 days and escalate non-completion to the function head and, for producers, to the Producer Compliance Manager for appointment action.
Record completion by function and by producer agency as the evidence for the pillar.
checklist.done: annual role-differentiated training reaches employees and covered-product producers with completion tracked and non-completion escalated.

checklist.step: Commission the independent test on its cycle
actions: Scope the independent test to the four pillars, CDD file quality, monitoring scenario coverage and tuning, SAR timeliness and the group-wide application to branches and subsidiaries.
Confirm the testers have no operational role in the programme and no reporting line to the Financial Crime AML Officer, and record the independence confirmation.
Complete the test within the cycle - 12 months for higher-risk entities, no more than 24 months elsewhere - and issue the report with findings rated and management responses recorded.
Report the findings to the Board Audit Committee directly, not through the AML function.
Track remediation to closure with evidence, and re-test closed findings in the following cycle.
checklist.done: an independent test within the cycle is reported to the Board Audit Committee with rated findings, management responses and tracked remediation.

checklist.step: Apply the programme across branches and subsidiaries
actions: List every foreign branch and majority-owned subsidiary writing covered products with its local AML requirement and the standard it currently applies.
Where the local standard is weaker than the group standard, require the group standard, and record the gap analysis that proves it is being met.
Where local law prevents application - typically data-sharing restrictions - document the restriction, the additional measures applied and the notification to the group-wide supervisor.
Confirm the group information-sharing arrangement for AML purposes is documented and that the local Data Protection Officer has cleared the transfers.
Obtain an annual attestation from each entity's local compliance lead that the group programme is applied.
checklist.done: each branch and subsidiary holds a documented standard comparison and an annual attestation, with legal impediments and additional measures recorded.

checklist.step: Maintain the record-keeping the rules demand
actions: Set retention at 5 years after policy termination for CDD and identification records, and 5 years after the transaction for transaction records, with 7 years applied under group policy where longer.
Confirm records are retrievable by customer name, policy number and date range within the timeframe an examiner allows, and test a retrieval each quarter.
Keep SAR material and its supporting documents in restricted storage separate from the customer file, with an access log.
Confirm the retention label survives system migration by testing retrieval of a pre-migration record annually.
checklist.done: CDD, transaction and SAR records meet their retention rules, are retrievable on a tested quarterly basis and SAR material is access-logged.

checklist.step: Report programme health to the Board Audit Committee each quarter
actions: Report alert and case volumes, SAR filings and their timeliness, CDD file quality results, training completion and open independent testing findings with ageing.
Name the resourcing position explicitly against case volumes, since the designated officer's authority and resources are themselves a tested requirement.
Escalate any covered product operating outside the programme and any entity applying a weaker standard.
Have the minute record the committee's acceptance and any direction given.
checklist.done: each quarter's committee minute records programme metrics, the resourcing position and any escalated scope or standard gaps.

checklist.step: Prepare and rehearse the examination response pack
actions: Assemble the standing pack: current programme document, board minute with the officer designation, risk assessment, training completion by function, latest independent test report with responses, SAR log summary and the covered-product list.
Refresh the pack within 5 business days of any board approval or independent test issuance so it is never more than one cycle old.
Rehearse the document request drill annually by pulling ten randomly named customer files and timing retrieval.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel the handling rules for SAR material in any production, since SAR disclosure outside permitted channels is itself a violation.
checklist.done: a current examination pack exists, is refreshed within 5 business days of each cycle event and a timed retrieval drill is evidenced annually.

testing.step: Build the population of covered-product policies, cases and programme artifacts
actions: Extract every policy issued, in force or terminated in the period on a product classified as covered, with entity, issue date, owner type and premium.
Extract monitoring alerts, escalated cases and SAR filings for the period from the AML system with detection, escalation and filing dates.
Collect the programme document versions, board minutes, risk assessments, training records and independent test reports for the period.
Record extract dates, counts and queries in the workpaper before sampling.
testing.done: the policy, case and programme-artifact populations are extracted with dates and counts recorded before sampling.

testing.step: Reconcile the covered-product scope to the full product catalogue
actions: Take the full product catalogue and independently classify each product against the covered-product definition using its cash-value and investment features.
Compare to the recorded classification and list any product with a cash surrender value classified as not covered.
Trace policies written on any misclassified product and quantify how many were issued without covered-product CDD.
Treat a misclassified in-force product as a scope failure of the programme, not a single-file exception.
testing.done: the covered-product list is independently rebuilt from product features and any misclassified product is quantified by policies affected.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of PEP and enhanced-due-diligence relationships, 100% of escalated cases where no SAR was filed, and 100% of SARs filed in the period.
Take 40 covered-product policies at random with a recorded seed, stratified across entity, product and distribution channel, plus 25 claim payouts.
Record population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every open independent-testing finding as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all EDD relationships, all not-filed escalations and all SARs, stratified across entities and channels.

testing.step: Test the four pillars against dated evidence
actions: Open the board minute and confirm it approves the current programme version by number and names the designated officer by name and title, dated within the last 12 months.
Confirm the risk assessment is dated within the last 12 months and was refreshed on any material product or market change in the period.
Recompute the interval since the last independent test against the 12- and 24-month cycle for each entity by risk rating.
Compute training completion by function against the 98% threshold and separately for appointed producers selling covered products.
testing.done: each pillar is evidenced by a dated artifact, with intervals recomputed and training completion measured against the threshold.

testing.step: Test CDD file completeness on the sampled policies
actions: For each sampled policy confirm the file holds verified identity for insured, owner and payer, with the verification evidence dated on or before the issue date.
Where the owner is corporate or a trust, confirm beneficial owners at the 25% threshold and the controlling person were identified and verified.
Confirm the source of funds and the customer risk rating were recorded at issue and that the periodic refresh date has not passed unactioned.
Treat any verification evidence dated after issue as a failure, since post-issue CDD does not meet the pre-acceptance requirement.
testing.done: each sampled file is tested for pre-issue identity verification, beneficial-owner identification, source of funds and a live refresh date.

testing.step: Test enhanced due diligence and senior approvals
actions: For each PEP or higher-risk relationship confirm documented source of wealth, not only source of funds, and read the documents relied on.
Confirm a written senior approval exists and pre-dates policy acceptance or the continuation decision.
Confirm the customer risk rating in the AML system matches the risk indicators in the file and that monitoring scenarios applicable to that rating are switched on for the customer.
List relationships rated standard whose file shows PEP or higher-risk indicators as rating failures.
testing.done: every sampled higher-risk relationship shows documented source of wealth, a pre-acceptance senior approval and a rating consistent with the file.

testing.step: Recompute SAR timeliness and test not-filed decisions
actions: For each SAR recompute calendar days from initial detection to filing and compare to the 30-day (or 60-day, where no subject was identified) deadline, listing every breach with days over.
Confirm the BSA identifier is recorded and the filed narrative covers who, what, when, where and why.
For each escalated case with no SAR, read the not-file rationale against the suspicion standard and reach an independent view.
Treat a not-file decision documented only as 'no suspicion' with no analysis as a fail, and escalate any case you would have filed.
testing.done: SAR timeliness is recomputed against the deadline and every not-filed escalation carries an independently reviewed, reasoned rationale.

testing.step: Test monitoring scenario coverage and feed integrity
actions: Compare the live scenario inventory to the typology list in the risk assessment and list typologies with no scenario.
Reconcile the transactions loaded into the monitoring system for three sample days to the policy administration and payment records for the same days.
Review every threshold change in the period for an approval and before-and-after alert volume evidence, and flag changes that reduced alert volumes without analysis.
Test that scenarios applicable to high-risk customers actually fire for them by tracing five high-risk customers' transactions through the scenario logic.
testing.done: scenario coverage is matched to typologies, the feed reconciles for sample days, and unapproved or unanalysed threshold changes are listed.

testing.step: Test the group-wide application to branches and subsidiaries
actions: Take the group entity list and confirm each covered-product entity holds a current standard comparison and an annual attestation from its local compliance lead.
For two entities test a sample of local CDD files against the group standard rather than the local minimum.
Confirm every documented legal impediment names the additional measures applied and the notification made to the group-wide supervisor.
List any entity applying a weaker standard with no documented impediment as a group programme failure.
testing.done: each covered-product entity evidences the group standard through attestation and file testing, with impediments and additional measures documented.

testing.step: Log exceptions, obtain independent sign-off and conclude
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, policy or case reference, the pillar or requirement failed and the regulatory exposure, assigning a root cause from a fixed list (scope misclassified, CDD incomplete at issue, EDD approval missing, SAR late, scenario gap, testing overdue, group standard not applied) with an owner and remediation date.
Compute the pillar compliance position, CDD file completeness rate, training completion rate and SAR on-time rate against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, referencing the file testing and recomputation workpapers.

Have the independent reviewer, who holds no operational role in the AML programme and does not report to the Financial Crime AML Officer, sign the workpaper; report directly to the Board Audit Committee and file the workpaper indexed by entity and period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states pillar, CDD, training and SAR rates, with every exception owned and reported directly to the Board Audit Committee.
